jobs.title: Audit Policy Analyst, Post-Acute Services
jobs.excerpt: Machinify is a leading healthcare intelligence company with expertise across the payment continuum, delivering unmatched value, transparency, and efficiency to health plan clients across the country.
jobs.description:
Machinify is a leading healthcare intelligence company with expertise across the payment continuum, delivering unmatched value, transparency, and efficiency to health plan clients across the country. Deployed by over 85 health plans, including many of the top 20, and representing more than 270 million lives, Machinify brings together a fully configurable and content-rich, AI-powered platform along with best-in-class expertise. We’re constantly reimagining what’s possible in our industry, creating disruptively simple, powerfully clear ways to maximize financial outcomes and drive down healthcare costs.

As part of the Complex Payment Solutions (CPS) Team, the Audit Policy Analyst, Post-Acute Services serves as the subject matter expert for durable medical equipment (DME), home health, and home infusion therapy claims across government and commercial lines of business. This role leads the development, maintenance, testing, and optimization of post-acute payment integrity audit concepts and partners with operations, clinical, client services, and technology teams to ensure each concept is built, validated, and maintained in alignment with coding standards, coverage and medical necessity criteria, documentation requirements, and client-specific payer policy.

The ideal candidate brings authoritative, hands-on knowledge of how post-acute services are ordered, documented, billed, and paid, including DME MAC policy, the Home Health Patient-Driven Groupings Model (PDGM), and the Medicare home infusion therapy benefit. This role requires strong analytical and communication skills, a track record of leading audit concept development, the ability to manage complex workflows independently, and the ability to mentor a team of subject matter experts.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Policy Development and Maintenance

  • Develop new post-acute audit concepts for DME, home health, and home infusion therapy claims, including research, data and claim analysis, rule documents, and code lists.
  • Review and update existing audit concepts on required periodic cycles or in response to client or regulatory changes, including quarterly HCPCS updates, DMEPOS fee schedule updates, and annual Home Health PPS final rules.
  • Monitor and interpret changes to National Coverage Determinations (NCDs), DME MAC Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) and Policy Articles, the Medicare Benefit Policy and Claims Processing Manuals, and CMS transmittals, and document their impact on existing concepts.
  • Interpret and apply client-specific commercial and Medicaid payer policy, including home infusion per diem billing, DME rental and purchase rules, and prior authorization requirements.
  • Approach for Medicaid audit development in DME and Home Health across multiple states and managed care contracts, the audit program should be built around both federal requirements and state-specific contract obligations.

Policy Testing and Validation

  • Perform QA reviews of audit concepts to confirm compliance with regulatory, coding, and citation changes and to confirm updates are applied timely.
  • Validate concept logic against post-acute billing rules, including DME capped rental and oxygen payment rules, modifier requirements (e.g., KX, GA, GZ, RR, NU, UE), home health 30-day period and LUPA logic, and home infusion therapy visit and drug billing.
  • Identify discrepancies in concept performance and drive resolution with clinical, coding, and operations teams.
  • Ensure audit concepts are validated against current coding guidelines, payment methodologies, and payer policy prior to deployment.

Operational and Workflow Support

  • Manage, track, and progress multiple tasks across concurrent audit concept workflows with a high degree of accuracy and quality, delivering results on time.
  • Ensure audit teams apply post-acute policies consistently and correctly across auditing platforms and client programs.
  • Serve as the escalation point for auditors and clinical reviewers on complex DMEPOS, home health, and home infusion documentation and coverage questions.

Training and Documentation

  • Create training materials, job aids, and reference tools for new and existing post-acute audit concepts, including documentation checklists for orders, face-to-face encounters, proof of delivery, homebound status, and plans of care.
  • Maintain organized, accessible documentation of post-acute audit policies and concept updates.

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Client Support

  • Respond to client inquiries and provide subject matter support to client services for presentations, provider disputes, and escalations involving post-acute claims.
  • Partner with operations, clinical teams, technology, and internal stakeholders to support policy execution and drive concept quality.
  • Provide expert feedback to improve policy usability, accuracy, and effectiveness across the organization.

Performance Monitoring and Analytics

  • Monitor concept performance and provide statistical analysis to drive scoring and selection for new and existing post-acute audit concepts.
  • Identify trends in DME, home health, and home infusion claim data, such as utilization outliers, high-cost supply patterns, and billing inconsistencies across care settings, and recommend actions to optimize audit yield and accuracy.

Process Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to improve audit concept workflows, documentation processes, and policy management practices.
  • Support ongoing enhancements to concept tracking, QA processes, and cross-functional coordination.

Other Duties

  • Perform additional responsibilities and ad hoc projects as assigned to meet business needs.

Job Requirements

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in nursing, health administration, business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Minimum 5+ years of progressive experience in DME, home health, and/or home infusion therapy, including direct experience in payment integrity, claims auditing, or provider-side billing and compliance.
  • Equivalent experience of 3+ years in post-acute claims auditing and recovery auditing.
  • Registered Nurse or Certified Coder holding a nationally recognized credential (RHIA, RHIT, AHIMA, AAPC, or equivalent) required.
  • Home health coding (HCS-D, BCHH-C), OASIS (COS-C), or infusion nursing (CRNI) credential preferred.

Knowledge, Skills, and Expertise

  • Demonstrated depth and breadth of knowledge across post-acute coding systems and payment methodologies, including ICD-10-CM, HCPCS Level II, CPT, and HIPPS, the DME fee schedule and Competitive Bidding Program, Home Health PPS under PDGM, and the Medicare home infusion therapy benefit.
  • Deep understanding of DME MAC jurisdictions, LCDs, Policy Articles, and supplier documentation requirements, including Standard Written Orders, face-to-face encounters, proof of delivery, continued need, and the DME Required Prior Authorization List.
  • Deep understanding of Medicare home health conditions of payment, including homebound status, face-to-face encounter, certification and recertification, plan of care, OASIS assessment, and the Notice of Admission.
  • Broad knowledge of provider billing guidelines, payer reimbursement policies, medical necessity criteria, and claim adjudication standards for post-acute services.
  • Expert knowledge of clinical documentation requirements and audit concept development for post-acute claim types.
  • Strong experience in data utilization and statistical analysis, including driving scoring and selection for audit concepts.
  • Progressive healthcare data analysis experience, including gathering and documenting requirements for projects of diverse scope and complexity.
  • Experience developing clinical content, policy documentation, and training resources.
  • Proven ability to communicate effectively with all levels of the organization, with diverse teams, and with external clients.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with strong attention to detail.
  • Excellent critical thinking and analytical skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent workflows independently and in a remote environment, delivering results on time.

Computer Equipment and Software

  • Proficient in Windows office systems, including the full Microsoft Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and Teams).
  • Advanced skills in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Familiarity with encoder and grouper applications, including the Home Health PDGM Grouper.
  • Experience working with various software platforms and collaborating with development teams.
  • Proven success in a remote working environment.

Equal Employment Opportunity at Machinify

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Machinify is an employment at will employer. We participate in E-Verify as required by applicable law. jobs.description:

About the Role

One of our company values is "Embrace Differences" and diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging are the principles guiding how we build our business and teams. We encourage interested candidates from all backgrounds to apply, even if you don't think they meet some expectations of the role.

jobs.excerpt: NBC is seeking a Director, Product - Sports and Programming Data to lead the product strategy, design, integration, and evolution of the data architecture that powers sports viewing experiences.
jobs.description:
NBC is seeking a Director, Product - Sports and Programming Data to lead the product strategy, design, integration, and evolution of the data architecture that powers sports viewing experiences. This role will serve as a strategic product leader and primary subject matter expert for sports data and programing architecture, responsible for translating complex data feeds into scalable, reliable, and fan-friendly digital experiences across web, mobile, connected TV, and emerging platforms. The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise in live sports data systems with a strong understanding of how sports information is consumed by fans, broadcasters, journalists, and internal stakeholders.

What You'll Do:

The role will work closely with engineering teams, product management, design, editorial, and operations groups to ensure accurate and compelling presentation of sports and programming information across digital platforms

  • Define and own sports data architecture solutions across multiple digital products.
  • Serve as the subject matter expert for international sports data ecosystems.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering and UX teams to translate complex sports datasets into intuitive user-facing experiences.
  • Own the strategy and roadmap for programming metadata platforms, from data ingestion and processing through distribution across digital products.
  • Ensure programming data is accurately mapped to and integrated with NBCU's existing metadata models and platform architecture.
  • Serve as the subject matter expert for programming data, including data providers, linear schedules, content taxonomy, and metadata architecture.
  • Drive alignment between external data providers, internal stakeholders, and engineering teams to continuously improve metadata coverage, accuracy, and usability.

Qualifications

  • Extensive experience of working with sports data platforms, sports technologies, or large-scale digital sports products.
  • Deep knowledge of international sports data models, event structures, schedules, athlete metadata, statistics, and results systems.
  • Experience integrating and interpreting complex programming data feeds.
  • Strong understanding of programming data systems, broadcast workflows, and competition operations.
  • Experience translating technical data structures into customer-facing experiences.

Preferred

  • Direct experience working with OBS data services, Olympic Games technology programs, or IOC information systems.
  • Experience with ODF, BDF, XML, JSON, GraphQL, and sports data APIs.
  • Experience working with data providers such as Stats Perform, Sportradar, Opta, Genius Sports, Gracenote, or equivalent.
  • Knowledge of Olympic and international federation competition formats.
  • Experience supporting large-scale live sporting events.
  • Familiarity with cloud-based data platforms and modern data engineering practices.
  • Experience with AI-assisted metadata enrichment, content tagging, and sports data discovery

Additional Requirements

  • This position is eligible for company sponsored benefits, including medical, dental and vision insurance, pension, paid leave, tuition reimbursement, and a variety of other discounts and perks. Learn more about the benefits offered by NBCUniversal by visiting the Benefits page of the Careers website. Salary range: EUR 95,000 - EUR 110,000 (bonus and long-term incentive eligible)

jobs.excerpt: Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP-BC) $125k - $145k/year Position Requirement: Full-Time FLSA Status: Exempt Location: Akron, OhioSalary:125K - 145K+Work from Home!
jobs.description:
Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP-BC) $125k - $145k/year

Position Requirement: Full-Time

FLSA Status: Exempt

Location: Akron, Ohio

Salary:

125K - 145K+

Work from Home! Competitive, negotiable salary! Work/life balance! Leadership and advancement opportunities!

Join a leading clinician-led behavioral health company today! OptiMindHealth (OMH) is expanding and seeking compassionate psychotherapists to join our team. Today, OMH provides superior behavioral health services to patients in Massachusetts and Colorado. Since 2016, we’ve specialized in serving both adult and adolescent patients in a supportive outpatient environment. Our practice strives to improve access to holistic and cost-effective mental health care while supporting our clinical staff in all aspects of their work. Our clinicians define this work as the perfect balance between flexibility and efficiency.

OMH offers a variety of part-time and/or full-time options to our clinicians. Packages can be customized towards every clinician’s needs. Packages can include some combination of:

· Competitive Salary

· Medical benefits

· Paid malpractice policy

· CEU reimbursement

· Paid time off (PTO) and paid holidays

· Productivity Bonuses in select areas

· Work-Life Balance

· Flexible Work Schedule

  • No extra on call work, simply cover the care for your own patients!

It is common for clinicians to diversify their work today. Therefore, OMH’s flexibility and part-time options are the perfect complement to your professional and/or personal commitments. You can feel secure that OMH will offer steady, consistent income throughout your tenure.

Work from or close to home:

With locations in Colorado and Massachusetts, OMH is continuing to expand into states around the country. OMH will work with you to identify the best “fit” and will provide everything you need to treat OMH patients remotely from the comfort of your home. Our interview process focuses on your skill sets, interest as well as geographic location to match you to the best available option to begin working with OMH. Ask to speak with our recruitment team today to identify the local office(s) in your area, as well as those offices that are being planned for launch. Of course, if you prefer to work from home, we also have fully remote positions available.

Responsibilities:

The Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP-BC) will participate in the integrated care team model at OMH. Outpatient behavioral health practices like OMH are getting more attention than ever before due to the emphasis on team approaches. Join OMH to perfect your skills in the emerging field of integrated behavioral health care. The interdisciplinary health care team includes physicians, psychiatric nurse practitioners, licensed clinical psychologists, and licensed mental health professionals (LCSW/LPC/LMFT/LMHC). OMH values clinical relationships between all provider levels and believes this coordinated, collaborative approach provides the highest level of care to the patients we are privileged to serve.

Customize the care for each patient:

Our clinicians have the unique ability to customize the care for each and every individual patient. You will have the autonomy to determine how often you see a patient as well as the appropriate length of time spent with each patient. Medication management and individual psychotherapy are the most common forms of clinical work performed at OMH, but our clinicians also perform family therapy, group therapy, and psychological testing as needed and/or appropriate to a wide range of presenting problems of our patients.

Pick your own schedule!

  • Enjoy the freedom to create your own custom schedules with the perfect work/life balance.
  • Typically, clinicians work between Mondays – Fridays somewhere between the hours of 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM.

Focus on the patient’s care without the hassle or any additional on-call responsibilities. Simply cover the care for you own patients! Our medical staff and clinical psychotherapists focus on the patient’s care and our back-office support team handles the rest. This allows our clinicians time to be spent where it should be; with the patients they serve. Each clinician is responsible for clinical care and documentation following treatment sessions. Once that’s complete, our support team will handle all billing, collections, credentialing, etc. Once you leave the office for the day, your time is yours. No additional on-call responsibilities and no time spent wasted dealing with insurance companies.

Interested in benefits?

Full-time clinicians are eligible for medical health benefits. Please speak with the recruitment team to obtain additional specifics on benefits.

Leadership & Advancement:

OMH is a growing, clinician-led company. Our Site Supervisors are geographically dispersed throughout the areas we work in order to have staff leaders available to every clinician. Talk with our recruitment team today about the advancement opportunities to become senior psychotherapists and/or site supervisors.

Licensure, Education & Experience:                                    

Licensure in Colorado and/or Massachusetts as a Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner with experience working with persons who have various behavioral health issues such as, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, personality disorders, substance misuse, and other psychiatric impairments under the supervision of a consulting psychiatrist(s).  We welcome new graduates!

Preferred: Successful completion of PMHNP-BC exam(s).

This document represents the major duties, responsibilities, and authorities of this job, and is not intended to be a complete list of all tasks and functions. Other duties may be assigned as well. 

Salary: $125,000 – $145,000 / year

jobs.title: Salesforce Solution Architect
jobs.excerpt: About The Position As the Salesforce Solution Architect at KIPP Foundation, you will serve as the primary technical authority for our Salesforce platforms—a hands-on architect and principal developer responsible for platform strategy, enterprise solution design, and delivery across KIPP’s national Salesforce ecosystem.
jobs.description:
About The Position

As the Salesforce Solution Architect at KIPP Foundation, you will serve as the primary technical authority for our Salesforce platforms—a hands-on architect and principal developer responsible for platform strategy, enterprise solution design, and delivery across KIPP’s national Salesforce ecosystem.

You will partner with technology leadership, administrators, developers, product owners, business stakeholders, and implementation partners to deliver scalable solutions across NPSP, Nonprofit Cloud, Experience Cloud, Data Cloud, Agentforce/Einstein AI, enterprise integrations, and DevOps governance, while maintaining high engineering standards, strong platform governance, and long-term sustainability.

Responsibilities

Solution Architecture & Integrations

• Design and implement scalable Salesforce solutions aligned with KIPP’s enterprise technology strategy, translating business requirements into durable, high-quality technical architectures.
• Architect integrations across Salesforce, Azure, SQL Server, and third-party systems using REST/SOAP/Bulk APIs, Platform Events, Change Data Capture, and middleware patterns, while defining API standards, security controls, and monitoring practices
• Provide technical oversight, architecture review, and code review for external contractors and consulting partners, ensuring solution quality, maintainability, security, and alignment with KIPP standards.

Platform Strategy & Governance

• Own the Salesforce platform roadmap including org strategy, sandbox and environment management, security model, data architecture, deployment processes, and release management.
• Establish data governance standards including data modeling, data quality, master data management, and platform best practices across the organization.
• Monitor platform health through capacity planning, license optimization, performance tuning, and proactive management of technical debt.
• Apply Salesforce Well-Architected Framework principles across solution design, development, and contractor-delivered implementations.

NPSP & Nonprofit Cloud

• Own KIPP’s Salesforce NPSP architecture including donor and constituent data models, fundraising workflows, engagement automation, and nonprofit best practices.
• Lead planning and execution strategy for migration from NPSP to Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud, including data mapping, gap analysis, coexistence planning, and phased transition roadmap.
• Define nonprofit-specific customization standards aligned with Salesforce’s nonprofit roadmap and KIPP’s operational needs.

Technical Leadership & Delivery

• Serve as the hands-on architect and principal developer for KIPP's Salesforce platform — a senior individual contributor who leads through technical expertise, engineering standards, and cross-functional influence. You will provide architectural direction and quality oversight to external contractors and consulting partners..
• Make key architectural decisions on declarative versus programmatic solutions based on governor limits, scalability, performance, maintainability, and long-term platform health.
• Lead engineering standards across code architecture, trigger frameworks, CI/CD pipelines, source control, deployment automation, testing, and release management.
• Act as the primary escalation point for complex production issues and Zendesk escalations, including performance bottlenecks, integration failures, data integrity incidents, end-user support, and platform troubleshooting, ensuring timely resolution and minimal business disruption.

AI, Data Cloud & Experience Cloud

• Design and implement Agentforce, Einstein AI, Einstein Copilot, and prompt engineering solutions with responsible AI guardrails including controls, transparency, and bias mitigation.
• Architect Data Cloud strategies for unified profiles, audience segmentation, AI-driven personalization, and real-time activation across constituent and staff experiences.
• Design Experience Cloud portals, communities, and self-service solutions using LWC, personalization, and mobile-responsive best practices.

Skills and Mindsets

  • Mission and Student Focus: Demonstrates passion and commitment to KIPP’s mission and possesses the desire and ability to uphold KIPP’s Core Values: Focus on Excellent Results, Collective Impact, and Courageous Action.

  • Self-Management: Demonstrated record of setting ambitious goals and achieving them with consistency; uses quantitative and qualitative data to define goals, monitor progress, address obstacles, and adjust plans so systems and workstreams achieve desired outcomes.

  • Work Management: Sets a clear vision for complex bodies of technical work, develops agile project plans, manages competing priorities, and ensures work is replicable through clear documentation, sustainable processes, and high-quality delivery standards.

  • Process Management: Develops, codifies, and improves cross-team processes that support Salesforce platform governance, release management, data quality, integration standards, and long-term system sustainability.

  • Data-Driven Actions and Decisions: Defines the right metrics to evaluate platform health, data quality, adoption, technical debt, delivery performance, and business outcomes; ensures critical technical decisions and recommendations are grounded in reliable data and evidence.

  • Problem-Solving: Addresses root causes of complex Salesforce, integration, data, and production issues; anticipates downstream risks; removes obstacles; and develops scalable, sustainable solutions that support end users and organizational priorities.

  • Communication and Change Management: Translates complex technical concepts into clear, compelling narratives and actionable plans for technical and non-technical audiences; supports change adoption through stakeholder engagement, documentation, training, and transparent communication.

  • Collaboration: Builds productive working relationships with technology leaders, administrators, developers, product owners, business stakeholders, implementation partners, and external consultants to deliver durable solutions aligned to shared goals.

  • Technical Expertise: Demonstrates deep Salesforce architecture and development expertise across NPSP, Nonprofit Cloud, Experience Cloud, Data Cloud, Agentforce/Einstein AI, Apex, LWC, Flows, APIs, integrations, DevOps, security, and platform governance.

Experience and Qualifications
• 8+ years of enterprise technology experience, with 3+ years specifically in a Salesforce Architect or Lead Developer role.
• Deep expertise in Salesforce architecture across Experience Cloud, Data Cloud, NPSP, and Nonprofit Cloud, with strong understanding of scalability, governor limits, and enterprise solution design.
• Expert proficiency in Apex, LWC, Flows, SOQL/SOSL, Salesforce APIs, and enterprise integrations using event-driven architecture patterns.
• Experience with LDV strategies, data modeling, migration planning, platform optimization, and Salesforce Well-Architected Framework principles.
• Hands-on experience with Agentforce, Einstein AI, Einstein Copilot, Prompt Builder, and AI-driven workflow automation.
• Strong stakeholder management, communication, and ability to translate strategy into technical roadmaps.

Tools and Technologies
• Salesforce: Experience Cloud, Data Cloud, NPSP, Nonprofit Cloud, Agentforce, Einstein AI
• Development: Apex, LWC, Flows, SOQL/SOSL, JavaScript, C#/.NET
• Integration: REST/SOAP/Bulk APIs, Platform Events, CDC, MuleSoft
• DevOps: Salesforce DX, Git, CI/CD, deployment automation
• Platforms: Azure, SQL Server, Tableau, Salesforce CLI, VS Code

Certifications
Required: Salesforce Certified Application Architect or System Architect, Platform Developer II
Preferred: Salesforce Certified Data Architect, Integration Architect, Nonprofit Cloud Consultant

Work Conditions

  • Travel requirements: Basic Travel Expectations: Up to 5% (up to 10 days per year)

  • Job Type: Full time, Exempt

Location

This role is required to work full time in the United State. It is preferred, but not mandatory for this role to be based out of a KIPP Foundation office. This role has the option of working from a remote office full-time. KIPP Foundation offices are in NYC and Chicago.

Compensation and Benefits

In compliance with local law, we are disclosing the compensation, or a range thereof, for roles in locations where legally required. Actual salaries will vary based on several factors, including but not limited to external market data, internal equity, and relevant experience. The salary range for this position is $155,000-$170,000. In addition, KIPP Foundation provides a variety of benefits to employees, including: 

  • 25 holidays for + 18 days additional flexible PTO days (flexible PTO increases to 23 days for years 3 and 4 and to 28 days for years 5+).

  • 100% paid parental leave

  • 100% coverage of the premium for employee and 75% for employee + family’s medical/dental/vision plans.

  • Wellness benefits such as fitness reimbursements, discounted tickets to theme parks/attractions, backup care support for children and adults/elders, and our employee assistance program

  • Finance Security benefits include such as a 401K retirement plan with 4% match, employer-sponsored legal plans, life/disability insurance, and flexible spending accounts

KIPP Foundation embraces the opportunity to build a workforce that reflects the diversity of the students and communities with whom we work and the world that’s around them. Being an equal opportunity employer means that we take seriously our responsibility to consider qualified candidates on the basis of merit, without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, mental or physical disability, and genetic information, marital status, citizenship status, military status, protected veteran status or any other category protected by law. 

About the Organization

KIPP Public Schools is a national network of tuition-free public charter schools that prepares students with the skills and confidence to create the future they want for themselves, their communities, and us all. We are a network of 279 schools, nearly 16,500 educators, and nearly 210,000 students and alumni.

Our mission: Together with families and communities, we create joyful, academically excellent schools that prepare students with the skills and confidence to pursue the paths they choose—college, career, and beyond—so they can lead fulfilling lives and build a more just world.

Our vision: Every child grows up free to create the future they want for themselves and their communities.

The KIPP Foundation is a nonprofit organization that supports KIPP public charter schools across the country. The KIPP Foundation helps to develop outstanding educators to lead KIPP schools; provides tools and resources for excellent teaching and learning; promotes innovation; and facilitates the exchange of insights and ideas across KIPP and other public schools and organizations.

About Our Values:

Excellent Results for Students: We value results over effort and know that our work is not finished until all students thrive. We maintain high expectations for self, team, and students. We drive outcomes by operating with agility, removing barriers, differentiating support, and prioritizing student-centered solutions—especially for those at the margins.

Collective Impact: We are one team. We win together. We embody a one-team mindset by working collaboratively across teams, aligning goals, and leveraging the strengths of all teammates. We build trust-based relationships and ensure inclusive decision-making by engaging those closest to the work. We provide clarity through simple, repeatable systems and goals that enable transformational outcomes.

Courageous Action: Our belief in what we can achieve is unwavering, fueling our optimism and commitment to overcome any challenge. We demonstrate an unwavering belief in students' potential and a commitment to addressing systemic inequities. We approach challenges with resilience, a solutions-focused mindset, and adaptability. We foster a psychologically safe environment centered on trust and accountability where feedback is encouraged. We leverage data to reflect on progress, own setbacks, celebrate successes, and continuously improve to maximize impact.

About Us

The North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) is one of the largest, most complex agencies in the state, and has approximately 17,000 employees. It is responsible for ensuring the health, safety, and well-being of all North Carolinians, providing human service needs for special populations including individuals who are deaf, blind, developmentally disabled, and mentally ill, and helping poor North Carolinians achieve economic independence.


Description of Work

The Audit Resolution Consultant supports North Carolina Medicaid by computing erroneous payments of state and federal shares resulting from eligibility errors made by county departments of social services.

The position examines county eligibility error findings across state and federal audits to accurately determine county overpayment amounts and reviews claims data using NCTracks to verify service codes, amounts, and eligibility histories. It coordinates with the Local Government Commission, local Certified Public Accountants, and the Office of the State Auditor to establish functional audit requirements and strengthen audit processes.

The Audit Resolution Consultant operates within the Office of Compliance & Program Integrity and ensures financial accountability by applying statutory requirements under N.C. General Statute 108A‑25.1A. This position contributes to Medicaid program integrity by supporting accurate reconciliation of erroneous benefit issuances and claims payments.

Key Duties Include:

– Compute erroneous Medicaid payment amounts by determining state and federal financial responsibility based on county eligibility errors.

– Examine county eligibility error findings across state and federal audits to identify and calculate county overpayment amounts.

– Review claims payment data in NCTracks to verify service codes, claims amounts, and beneficiary eligibility history.

– Analyze erroneous Medicaid benefit issuance data to determine when payments were made for ineligible individuals, dates, or amounts.

– Coordinate with the Local Government Commission, local CPAs, and the Office of the State Auditor to establish audit requirements and improve service provision.

– Liaise with internal and external stakeholders to support functional audit activities and ensure compliance with statutory requirements.

– Document audit findings and payment calculations to support financial reconciliation processes.

– Support oversight activities required under N.C. General Statute 108A‑25.1A to ensure counties are held financially responsible for erroneous Medicaid issuances.

– Evaluate audit outcomes and identify opportunities to strengthen Medicaid error‑detection and accountability processes.

– Maintain accurate records of audit data, calculations, and correspondence to support program integrity and reporting needs.

Knowledge Skills and Abilities/Management Preferences

Salary Grade Range: $52,592.00 - $92,036.00


Candidates now meet the minimum qualifications of a position if they meet the minimum education and experience listed on the vacancy announcement.


The Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs)/ Management Preferences are not required. Applicants who possess the following skills are preferred:


  • Demonstrated experience navigating, evaluating, and analyzing NCFAST system decisions and functionality at an intermediate or higher proficiency level, with at least three years of documented use.

  • Track record navigating and evaluating NCTracks (MMIS) system functionality to obtain and interpret service codes, claims amounts, and beneficiary eligibility history, supported by at least three years of experience.

  • Documented experience reviewing and interpreting state or county Medicaid eligibility audit findings to support accurate assessment of erroneous payments and overpayment determinations.

  • Proven success communicating effectively with internal and external stakeholders to support audit coordination, error resolution, and program integrity activities.

  • Established experience analyzing Medicaid claims and eligibility discrepancies using system‑derived data to support accurate computation of erroneous payments and audit outcomes.



The Posting Will Close At 11:59 P.M. The Night Before The End Date

This Position Is Funded In Part Through Federal Funds

This Position Is Eligible For A Fully Remote Work Option

About the NC Division of Health Benefits:

The Division of Health Benefits (DHB) within NCDHHS is committed to advancing innovative solutions that improve health, promote well-being and foster independence for all North Carolinians. DHB manages and oversees North Carolina Medicaid and other programs that provide access to services and supports for parents, children, seniors, people with intellectual / developmental disabilities, and behavioral health, substance use and traumatic brain injury disorders. With a budget over $27 billion in state and federal funds per fiscal year, DHB ensures that more than 108,000 enrolled providers are reimbursed for delivering covered services to 3.1 million beneficiaries.

jobs.description:
Staff Platform Engineer - Earthly Lunar

Write production software, design the cloud architecture behind it, and own how it runs in the real world.

About Earthly Lunar

Earthly Lunar is a guardrails engine for the AI era. Engineering organizations use it to turn their standards for quality, security, and compliance into automated checks across their repositories and CI/CD pipelines. Teams get feedback directly in pull requests, leaders can see where standards aren't being met, and compliance evidence is collected as the work happens. The standards apply whether a developer or an AI agent writes the code.

We're a small, AI-native team backed by Innovation Endeavors and Work-Bench, with angels including Jeff Dean, the CEOs of Datadog, Cockroach Labs, and Dash0, the founder of Sentry, and the creators of Elixir, Pandas, and Ruff/uv. We're building for enterprise engineering teams with complex environments and high expectations for reliability.

The role

We're looking for someone who is an excellent software engineer and an excellent cloud engineer. You can design and build a substantial backend feature in Go, work through the architecture it needs, deploy it safely, and debug it when production behaves differently from the test environment.

You'll work on Lunar's core product and the infrastructure that runs it, across our hosted service and customer-managed deployments. That includes backend services, deployment automation, Kubernetes, and the operational work that makes enterprise software dependable.

This is a staff-level individual contributor role. You'll stay hands-on while helping decide what we build, making architectural calls, and leading substantial projects through to production. We want someone whose judgment improves the whole team's work, not just their own code.

What you'll do

  • Write and maintain production Go code in Lunar's backend and supporting services. Own features from design and testing through deployment and ongoing operation.

  • Design and evolve our AWS architecture and Kubernetes infrastructure. Make deliberate trade-offs around reliability, security, performance, cost, and how much complexity a small team can support.

  • Build reusable Terraform modules, Helm charts, and deployment tooling. Make provisioning, upgrades, and recovery repeatable for both our hosted service and customer-managed installations.

  • Improve production reliability: useful metrics and alerts, capacity planning, backups and tested recovery, safe rollouts, and clear rollback paths. Participate in incident response and fix the causes of recurring problems.

  • Debug across the stack. Follow a failure through Go code, a database query, container behavior, Kubernetes networking, or cloud infrastructure rather than stopping at a team boundary.

  • Improve CI/CD and the development environment so engineers can test realistic changes and ship frequently without making production fragile.

  • Work with our forward deployed engineers and customer platform teams on difficult deployment and scale problems. Turn what we learn into product improvements that help every customer.

  • Lead technical design and code reviews, mentor teammates, and document decisions well enough that other engineers can maintain what you build. Keep solutions proportionate to the problem.

  • Build and manage AI-assisted engineering workflows for implementation, review, testing, and operational investigation. Make useful workflows repeatable for the team, with appropriate access controls and checks on their output.

What we're looking for

You need substantial software engineering experience and deep production infrastructure experience, plus extensive use of AI in your engineering work.

  • Strong Go and software engineering fundamentals. You've designed, shipped, and maintained production services, not only infrastructure scripts. You're comfortable with concurrency, APIs, testing, performance work, and debugging distributed systems.

  • Deep AWS experience. You've made and lived with cloud architecture decisions involving networking, IAM, compute, storage, and managed databases. You understand failure modes, isolation boundaries, and cost.

  • Extensive Kubernetes experience. You've built and operated production clusters and workloads, handled upgrades, and debugged real failures. You understand scheduling, networking, storage, RBAC, resource management, and Helm beyond following an installation guide.

  • Extensive Terraform experience. You've designed reusable modules and managed production infrastructure through code, including state, environment separation, drift, and safe changes to existing resources.

  • Strong operational instincts. You're comfortable with Linux, Docker, networking, and troubleshooting under pressure. You've taken responsibility for systems after launch and made them easier to operate over time.

  • Experience with production data and observability systems. You can operate and troubleshoot PostgreSQL or comparable SQL databases, object storage such as S3, and metrics, logs, and traces using tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, or OpenTelemetry.

  • Extensive experience using and managing AI workflows. AI coding tools and agents are part of your daily work. You build your own workflows, supply the context and tools they need, and manage their permissions, cost, and failure modes. You can explain how you verify generated code and infrastructure changes, and you remain responsible for the result.

  • A staff-level track record. You've taken ambiguous problems, chosen a practical approach, brought other engineers along, and delivered substantial changes that held up in production.

  • Clear communication and high ownership. You write useful design notes, can explain a trade-off to another engineer or a customer, and make progress without waiting for a detailed specification. You know when to ask for help.

Nice to have

  • Experience building developer tools, infrastructure products, or other B2B software used by engineering teams.

  • Experience shipping software into customer-managed Kubernetes environments, including restricted networks and enterprise security requirements.

  • Experience with gRPC and Protocol Buffers, queues and background workers, or distributed job execution.

  • Experience with GitOps and progressive delivery, Kubernetes operators, or multi-region systems.

  • Familiarity with software supply-chain security, policy as code, or compliance automation.

  • Experience as an early startup engineer or founder.

You might not be a fit if

  • You want an architecture or management role with little hands-on coding.

  • You enjoy operating infrastructure but don't want to build substantial production software, or want to write features without owning how they run.

  • You use AI only occasionally and aren't interested in building and managing your own engineering workflows.

  • You need a narrowly defined remit and a separate team to handle every issue outside it.

How we work

  • We're a small, senior team. You'll work directly with the founder and the founding engineers, with room to shape both the product and how we build it.

  • We use AI heavily and invest in the tools that make the team effective. Engineering judgment, testing, and review still matter.

  • We favor frequent, tested releases and straightforward systems over elaborate architecture we don't yet need.

  • Production ownership is shared engineering work. Part of your job is to make it less dependent on any one person.

  • We're remote, with overlapping working hours and written communication that lets people work independently.

Compensation & logistics

  • Base salary: $210,000-$260,000 (US base), depending on experience, plus equity.

  • Location: Remote (US & Canada).

  • Type: Full-time, staff-level individual contributor.

  • Production support: Incident response is part of the role.

Benefits

  • Healthcare, dental, and vision, including dependents (US & Canada)

  • Incentive stock plan

  • 401(k) / RRSP with employer matching (US & Canada)

  • Life insurance (US & Canada)

  • Credits for gym or activity equipment (US & Canada)

  • Fully remote work

  • Direct ownership of substantial engineering work in an early-stage company

Salary: 210K - 260K USD a year

Senior Tax Analyst

Songtradr US

VACANCY: FULL-TIME

Company Profile

Songtradr is the world’s largest B2B music technology company, offering end-to-end music licensing, rights management, and direct-to-fan solutions. Through strategic acquisitions like MassiveMusic and Bandcamp, Songtradr empowers music creators and enables brands to connect with audiences through the power of music.

Learn more at.

Team

Songtradr’s tax team is part of the global Finance and Control team and operates across all business units and group entities globally, including creative solutions, music licensing solutions and consumer solutions. There is strong exposure to US and global as well as direct and indirect taxes. The team is close knit with incredible opportunities to be involved in business and tax projects to build your tax and commercial skills. Ideal for someone who wants broad tax experience with autonomy, empowerment and on-the-job learning and development from keen mentors.

Job Description

We are seeking a Senior Tax Accountant with expert quantitative and analytical skills to interpret, organize, and report financial data, identify business issues and opportunities, and deliver sustainable solutions. The ideal candidate manages multiple overlapping deadlines, communicates effectively across all levels of the organization, and upholds professional accounting standards and regulatory requirements at all times. Strong English communication skills, proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Power BI, PowerPoint), and the ability to work collaboratively and stay effective under pressure are essential. This person also brings strong project planning abilities, strategic decision-making, critical thinking, and business acumen to support long-term organizational goals, while consistently adhering to company policies on attendance, confidentiality, and ethical conduct.

Main Job Duties

  • Partner with outside tax providers, as needed, including oversight of global corporate income tax filings, including review of draft returns, tax calendars, and work plans, etc. (Jurisdictions include US, UK, NL, AU, DE, etc)
  • Oversee indirect tax compliance functions, including sales tax, Canadian GST/QST, VAT, 1099, 1042, DAC 7, and W-8 BEN-E.
  • Prepare and review correspondence relating to various tax issues, including Sales Tax audits.
  • Assist accounting with the review of routine intercompany calculations and journal entries for the region.
  • Coordinate with internal departments to obtain data, reports, invoices, or other documentation as required.
  • Coordinate with accounting groups to ensure tax payments are allocated correctly; process journal entries or reclass entries as required.
  • Reconcile tax payments to ensure accuracy and proper allocation to internal accounts.
  • Research, analyze, interpret, document, and apply tax rules related to the sale of digital assets/services and the applicability of marketplace facilitator rules.
  • Continuously pursue professional education, updates, best practice information, and professional publications, and mentoring relationships to remain abreast of tax law developments that will impact the organization.
  • Work collaboratively with others within and outside of the Global Tax function to achieve goals, simplify processes, reduce costs, prevent loss, and to ensure that work is completed accurately and on time.

Desired Skills & Experience

  • Expert quantitative analysis skills, including the ability to interpret, analyze, organize, and report financial data.
  • Demonstrate capacity for gathering and scrutinizing data to identify issues, opportunities, patterns, and sustainable business solutions.
  • Ability to meet multiple, potentially overlapping, deadlines and adapt to changing priorities.
  • Ability to communicate effectively throughout the organization, including management, co-workers, and stores.
  • Demonstrated commitment to regulatory requirements; adheres consistently to all professional accounting standards and practices.
  • Proficient ability to communicate effectively with others using spoken and written English.
  • Proficient ability to remain effective under stress and respond to pressure in a manner acceptable to others and to the organization.
  • Proficient knowledge of Windows-based business computers and Microsoft Office programs; specifically, Excel, PowerBI, and PowerPoint
  • Expert project planning skills, including the ability to organize, prioritize and control job responsibilities in order to meet deadlines in an environment with overlapping and potentially conflicting priorities.
  • Consistently demonstrates a commitment to policies and procedures, including but not limited to, attendance, confidentiality, conflict of interest, and ethical responsibilities.

RELATED COMPETENCIES

  • Building Strategic Working Relationships – Developing and using collaborative relationships both within and outside the organization to facilitate the accomplishment of work goals.
  • Strategic Decision Making – Obtains information and identifies key issues and relationships relevant to achieving a long-range goal or vision; commits to a course of action to accomplish said goal or vision after developing alternatives based on technology assessments, logical assumptions, facts, available resources, constraints, and organizational values.
  • Critical Thinking and Analysis — Examines issues and ideas to identify viable, innovative business solutions in a large variety of situations with differing assumptions, contexts, and methods.
  • Global Business Acumen — Utilizing a broad, strategic understanding of how successful organizations grow, including the interdependencies between consumer, economic, financial, and legislative influences

Our Three Core Values

Lead with Music

It’s our compass and our passion. We champion creativity by putting artists, brands and fans first, balancing artistic integrity with bold commercial ambition.

Perform as One Band

United by purpose and trust. We aim high, knowing that collaboration, community, and doing it for the right reasons drives success for everyone.

Own Your Voice

We listen deeply and speak honestly. We value time, welcome diverse perspectives, and keep the rhythm of open, transparent communication alive.

Employment

Full time. What do you get in return? Inspiration, knowledge, career development, on top of our financial package. You’ll also be working with an international bunch of remarkable musically-infused individuals.

On this note, please know that Songtradr is an equal opportunities employer. Applicants will not be excluded on the grounds of sex, gender reassignment, pregnancy, maternity, race, marital status, diversity of thought, disability, age, religion, belief, or sexual orientation. And if you need any specific adjustments to be made throughout our recruitment process, please feel free to let us know.

If after reading this you know this is the perfect role for you, please apply via THIS LINK and make sure you include your resume and a brief summary of the professional achievement you are most proud of to date.   

We look forward to hearing from you!

60K - 85K+

Work from Home! Competitive, negotiable salary! Work/life balance! Leadership and advancement opportunities!

OMH offers a variety of part-time and/or full-time options to our clinicians. Packages can be customized towards every clinician’s needs. Join a leading clinician-led behavioral health company today! OptiMindHealth (OMH) is expanding and seeking compassionate psychotherapists to join our team and work remotely from the comfort of their home. Today, OMH provides superior behavioral health services patients in Massachusetts and Colorado. Since 2016, we’ve specialized in serving both adult and adolescent patients in a supportive outpatient environment. Our practice strives to improve access to holistic and cost-effective mental health care while supporting our clinical staff in all aspects of their work. Our clinicians define this work as the perfect balance between flexibility and efficiency.

Packages can include some combination of:

· Competitive Salary

· Medical benefits

· Paid malpractice policy

· CEU reimbursement

· Paid time off (PTO) and paid holidays

· Productivity Bonuses in select areas

· Work-Life Balance

· Flexible Work Schedule

· Remote work environment

  • No extra on call work, simply cover the care for your own patients!

It is common for clinicians to diversify their work today. Therefore, OMH’s "work from home" and part-time options are the perfect complement to your professional and/or personal commitments. You can feel secure that OMH will offer steady, consistent income throughout your tenure.

Work from or close to home:

With two convenient locations in Colorado and growing, OMH will work with you to identify the best “fit” and work-site location(s). Our interview process focuses on your skill sets, interest as well as geographic location to match you to the best available location. Ask to speak with our recruitment team today to identify the local office(s) in your area, as well as those offices that are being planned for launch. Of course, if your prefer to work from home, we also have remote positions available.

Responsibilities:

The psychotherapist will participate in the integrated care team model at OMH. Outpatient behavioral health practices like OMH are getting more attention than ever before due to the emphasis on team approaches. Join OMH to perfect your skills in the emerging field of integrated behavioral health care. The interdisciplinary health care team includes physicians, psychiatric nurse practitioners, licensed clinical psychologists, and licensed mental health professionals (LCSW/LPC/LMFT/LMHP). OMH values clinical relationships between all provider levels and believes this coordinated, collaborative approach provides the highest level of care to the patients we are privileged to serve.

Customize the care for each patient:

Our clinicians have the unique ability to customize the care for each and every individual patient. You will have the autonomy to determine how often you see a patient as well as the appropriate length of time spent with each patient. Individual psychotherapy is the most common clinical work performed, but our clinicians also perform family therapy, group therapy, and psychological testing as needed and/or appropriate to a wide range of presenting problems of our patients.

Pick your own schedule!

  • Enjoy the freedom to create your own custom schedules with the perfect work/life balance.
  • Typically, clinicians work between Mondays – Fridays somewhere between the hours of 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM.

Focus on the patient’s care without the hassle or any additional on-call responsibilities. Simply cover the care for you own patients! Our psychotherapists focus on the patient’s care and our back-office support team handles the rest. This allows our clinicians time to be spent where it should be; with the patients they serve. Each clinician is responsible for clinical care and documentation following treatment sessions. Once that’s complete, our support team will handle all billing, collections, credentialing, etc. Once you leave the office for the day, your time is yours. No additional on-call responsibilities and no time spent wasted dealing with insurance companies.

Interested in benefits?

Full-time clinicians are eligible to participate for medical health benefits. Please speak with the recruitment team to obtain additional specifics on benefits.

Leadership & Advancement:

OMH is a growing, clinician-led company. Our Site Supervisors are geographically dispersed throughout the areas we work in order to have staff leaders available to every clinician. Talk with our recruitment team today about the advancement opportunities to become senior psychotherapists and/or site supervisors.

Education & Licensure:

Completion of an accredited program with certification and licensure as a Licensed Mental Health Professional (LPC/LMFT/LCSW) in the state of Colorado with the ability to practice independently is required.

The specific statements shown in each section of this Job Description are not intended to be all-inclusive. They represent typical elements and criteria considered necessary to perform the job successfully. The job’s responsibilities/tasks may be modified and/or expanded over time. OMH will inform the employee when changes in the respective job description are made.

Salary: $60,000 – $85,000 / year

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. YOUR ROLE

You'll build the models that decide which carrier each auto insurance shopper sees on our click wall. The goal is to send every user to the carrier most likely to convert them, so carriers see our traffic convert and raise their bids. You'll also own the buying models behind our media spend, which are held to ROAS.

Carrier conversion data (quotes, policies and acquisition cost) is now coming back to us, and you'll be the one who puts it to work in production. The hard part is the data. Outcomes land weeks or months after the click, many sessions are sparse, the same shoppers come back, and the market drifts. Our bids also decide which users we win, so the model shapes the data it learns from next.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You frame problems directly with the business, find your own data, build and validate the model, and stay with it through deployment and monitoring. An ML engineer works alongside you on the production side. Auto insurance takes most of your time to start, and scope broadens to other verticals over time.

We're remote first, and most of the company works East Coast hours.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

By day 60, you run our insurance marketplace media buying on your own.

By the end of your first year:

  • Click wall serving that matches each user to the right carrier
  • Carrier conversion data running in production models
  • Automated marketplace bidding taken from proof of concept to scale
  • A clear approach for repeat users and sparse sessions
  • Production models that hold up through drift and changing objectives
  • Output the business trusts and uses without rework

  • 5+ years of hands-on applied data science with measurable business impact
  • Your models drove paid media decisions: spend, bidding or ad serving. Attribution and reporting alone don't qualify.
  • You built what's on your resume and can explain it down to the loss function and architecture choice, neural network fundamentals included
  • You see how today's bids shape tomorrow's training data, and you've handled late labels, sparse features or drift
  • You own models end to end: you find your own data, build through deployment and monitoring, and bring a point of view
  • Expert Python and SQL

NICE TO HAVES

  • Real ad budget spent in live auctions
  • Large-scale ranking or recommendation systems
  • Explaining tradeoffs to non-technical partners in plain terms
  • Designing for auction feedback loops, selection bias and exploration
  • Hands-on neural network work, such as embeddings of text, creative or user behavior
  • AWS for data science: ECS, S3, Athena, SageMaker
  • CI/CD deployment

Base salary is set according to market rates for the nearest major metro and varies based on Launch Potato’s Levels Framework. Launch Potato is a performance-driven company, which means once you are hired, future increases will be based on company and personal performance, not annual cost of living adjustments.

This role will be directly responsible for identifying & implementing system configuration setup and changes needed to deliver our global payroll services to clients. This position reports to our Global Payroll Manager.

Job Responsibilities

  • Maintains fundamental knowledge of Melita's services and clearly articulates all areas of global payroll compliance and HRIS topics relevant to the implementation process and payroll service.
  • Partners with the Melita & HRIS Implementation teams to configure and test the Payroll, Time & Attendance, and Time Off modules for new implementation clients. Performs parallel payroll testing to ensure payroll code calculation & taxation are working as expected per payroll regulations.

  • Loads client employee data to the payroll technology, completes paycheck history data mapping.

Maintains the master version of these resources and incorporates revisions submitted by the Global Payroll Manager following client training sessions.

  • Partners with the Payroll team to set up new payroll codes such as new earning, deduction, and memo codes in the payroll technology. Updates workflows in Salesforce CRM as needed to ensure they are properly used by the payroll team. Ensures changes are tested.
  • Performs a review of client benefit plan setups as they relate to payroll, aligned to the client's plan year, verifying that deduction codes in the payroll technology are correctly mapped to each benefit plan and that tax treatment is applied accurately.

jobs.description:
Founding Sales Development Representative (SDR) — AI & Zero Trust Security

Remote (US) · ET or CT time zone · [$60,000 base / $90,000 OTE] + equity

The short version: NetFoundry, the company behind OpenZiti, the world’s most used open source Zero Trust networking software, is hiring two founding SDRs to build NetFoundry's outbound engine. This is a hunter role selling Zero Trust connectivity into cybersecurity, cloud, and AI infrastructure teams. If you want to build the playbook instead of inheriting one and have ambition to become an AE, keep reading.

Why this matters now:

AI broke the network security model.

Agents, models, and APIs now need to reach data and systems scattered across clouds, data centers, edge sites, and customer environments. Every one of those connections is a new attack surface. VPNs, open inbound ports, and firewall rules were never designed for a world where the thing requesting access is a non-human identity that spun up four seconds ago.

NetFoundry replaces that model. Our Identity-First Connectivity™ platform delivers Zero Trust connectivity with no VPNs, no open inbound ports, and no firewall changes enabling enterprises to connect AI agents, APIs, and distributed workloads without exposing anything to the internet.

Enterprises use us to secure access to their APIs and agentic AI services, to run microsegmentation, and to simplify hybrid IT/OT segmentation. Software and IoT providers use us to reach workloads inside their customers' networks.

We were founded by the inventors and maintainers of OpenZiti, the world's most-used open source Zero Trust networking software. We're Series A, backed by SYN Ventures and Cisco Investments, headquartered in Charlotte, NC, and remote-first since day one.

The role:

We have one SDR today. We're hiring two more, and we're building the enterprise go-to-market motion around you.

That means the target account strategy, the sequences, the call openers, the objection handling, the way we mine our open source community for enterprise signal - isn't fully developed yet. You'll contribute to it working directly with our AEs, our marketing team, and GTM leadership that has built and exited multiple startups.

This is the right role if you want to be early. It's the wrong role if you want a machine that already runs.

A note on leads: This is an outbound focused role. Marketing supports you with content, campaigns, and intent data. Pieline starts with you, on the phone.

What you'll do:

  • Own outbound pipeline generation into a defined set of enterprise accounts — you build the list, you work the list
  • Cold call. Daily. This is the core of the job, not a footnote
  • Run multi-channel outbound across phone, email, and LinkedIn, with real personalization rather than merge fields
  • Run discovery that surfaces real pain: firewall and VPN sprawl, exposed APIs, OT segmentation projects, AI agents that need access to sensitive systems
  • Book qualified meetings for Account Executives and hit monthly and quarterly pipeline targets
  • Build account plans with AEs and multi-thread into security, networking, cloud, and platform teams
  • Act as our fastest feedback loop since you'll hear what the market says before anyone else. Leadership will change the messaging based on what you report.

What we're looking for:

  • Ambition to become an AE
  • 1–3 years in outbound SDR/BDR or inside sales, ideally in cybersecurity, SaaS, or enterprise technology
  • A track record you can put numbers to - activity, meetings booked, pipeline sourced, quota attainment
  • Genuine willingness to cold call, and the resilience to do it on the days it isn't working
  • Strong written communication; you can write an email a CISO would actually reply to
  • Comfort with technical buyers, and curiosity to learn what a firewall rule, a service mesh, and an AI agent actually are
  • Experience with CRM and sales engagement platforms (we run HubSpot)
  • Organized, coachable, and hard to discourage

Nice to have: Familiarity with Zero Trust or secure connectivity concepts; experience with open source or developer communities; account-based selling.

What you get:

  • A founding seat. You're among the first three SDRs at a company building a category, with direct access to GTM leadership and founders
  • A clear path to AE. Our SDR→AE path is 12-18 months for performers, and we'd rather promote you than hire around you
  • Competitive base with uncapped commission, plus meaningful equity — $60,000 base / $90,000 OTE (uncapped)
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision, plus expanded well-being benefits
  • Employer-paid life, AD&D, and short- and long-term disability
  • 401k with company match
  • Unlimited PTO and paid holidays
  • Learning & development budget, technology stipend, internet stipend, SWAG stipend
  • Remote-first with flexible hours, as a globally distributed team
Salary: $60,000 base/ $90,000 OTE (uncapped) + equity

Strategic Advisor, Change Management

Advisory | United States (Remote) | Full-Time | NAM

Who We Are: Front Office Transformation Experts

Bluprintx (BPX) is a global, AI-powered consultancy built to design and deliver the intelligent front office for CMO and CRO executives. We are private equity-backed and scaling fast, with 300 active customers across 10 countries and more than 1,750 implementations. We connect people, technology, and AI to turn fragmentation into performance, partnering with global leaders to modernize how marketing, CRM, content, AI & Data connect. At BPX, we hire operators and specialists who thrive at the intersection of commercial strategy and technical execution.

What We Do: Cutting Complexity Across the Front Office

We help the world's most ambitious companies, including Uber Eats, BNY, and Xerox, untangle the operational complexity that slows enterprise growth. As a Gold Adobe Solution Partner and Salesforce Summit Partner, we deliver strategy and implementation across the full front office. Our proprietary methodology builds sustainable enabled ecosystems that maximize ROI and accelerate speed to market. By embedding AI into commercial workflows, we help clients move faster and stay ahead.

The Role

You'll be the senior advisor our clients turn to when a transformation has to land with people, not just in platforms. The seat has two halves. First, you'll set change management strategy at enterprise level, working directly with C-suite and senior leaders to define how their organization moves to new ways of working across marketing, sales and service. Second, you'll run the change management programs inside our largest MarTech, CRM and data transformations, from impact assessment through to measured adoption in the months after go-live.

You'll work alongside other Senior Strategic Consultants, shaping each client's multi-year roadmap, our Solution Architects, who design the platform and integrations, and our Program Managers, who run delivery. You'll also help BPX grow, using change strategy as a lever to expand existing accounts and land new ones, and you'll shape how our change management capability develops across the global consulting team.

What you'll do

  • Set change management strategy for client organizations, aligning operating model, roles, governance and ways of working to the outcomes of a multi-year transformation roadmap.
  • Advise C-suite sponsors as a trusted, technology-agnostic voice, coaching executives on what their teams need from them at each stage and raising adoption risk early and plainly.
  • Run change programs on large MarTech transformations across Adobe, Salesforce, Braze and data platforms, owning the change workstream from impact assessment to sign-off.
  • Assess impact and readiness, mapping stakeholders, role and process changes and skills gaps, then holding go-live decisions to evidence that teams are ready.
  • Design communication, training and enablement plans for every audience, from frontline marketing and sales teams to senior leaders and centers of excellence.
  • Measure adoption and value after launch, defining the metrics, tracking usage in the live platforms and fixing what stalls early.
  • Lead workshops and design deliverables that give clients clear, practical guidance across people, process, data and technology.
  • Shape change in pre-sales, scoping approach, effort and commercial model when a transformation needs a dedicated change workstream, and spotting growth opportunities within existing accounts.
  • Build the BPX change practice, turning what works on each engagement into frameworks, templates and accelerators, and mentoring consultants across the global team.

What you'll bring

  • Ten or more years in strategy, transformation or change consulting, including several years leading change on enterprise CRM, MarTech or data programs.
  • Strategy and delivery range: a track record of both setting enterprise change strategy and running the programs that deliver it, across people, process, technology and data.
  • A proven change method such as Prosci ADKAR, ACMP standards or Kotter, applied on live client programs. Formal certification is an advantage.
  • Credibility at C-suite level, with evidence of building long-term advisory relationships and being the voice senior leaders trust when decisions get hard.
  • Large transformation experience in marketing, customer experience, digital or business transformation, working across multiple workstreams and senior governance.
  • Front office platform fluency across marketing automation, CRM, customer data platforms, journey orchestration and workflow tools, enough to know how they change someone's working day.
  • Comfort with adoption data: you define the metrics, read the dashboards and use them to decide what to fix.
  • Commercial instinct, with experience contributing to proposals, scoping and estimating work, and growing accounts through consultative selling.
  • Sector breadth across B2B and B2C. Experience in highly regulated industries such as financial services is a strong advantage.

Why this role, why now

Our clients are investing more than ever in their front office platforms, and the programs keep getting bigger. What decides whether that investment pays back is adoption, and that is where this seat sits. It's a new, senior role, so you'll set how BPX advises on change at the strategy table, how we run it on the ground, and the practice every program after yours will draw on.

Additional information

Location: Remote, United States.
