jobs.title: Director, Workforce Management
jobs.excerpt: The Clover Care Services organization delivers proactive support and care to our members through our clinical Clover Home Care teams, and quality improvement services to our aligned providers through our practice engagement team.
jobs.description:
The Clover Care Services organization delivers proactive support and care to our members through our clinical Clover Home Care teams, and quality improvement services to our aligned providers through our practice engagement team. Clover has built one of the most proactive, data-driven health care services platforms and is excited about how technology impacts our ability to bring transformative results to both patients and providers.

Clover Care Services is entering a significant period of clinical growth. As we scale our Clover Care Visit (CCV) team, we need a dedicated leader who can turn an ambitious hiring plan into a reliable, repeatable workforce engine—from recruiting pipeline and onboarding capacity through clinician readiness, productivity, and performance.

As the Director, Workforce Management, you will connect workforce planning, recruiting, onboarding, leadership capacity, and performance management into one operating system, giving the organization clear visibility into whether we are on pace and what needs to change when we are not.

As Director, Workforce Management, you will:

  • Own the CCV workforce plan end to end. Build and run the staffing strategy required to scale the clinician organization, translating long-range growth targets into weekly and monthly hiring, onboarding, and readiness goals.
  • Create visibility from candidate pipeline to “ready to visit.” Establish the operating metrics, forecasting, and reporting needed to understand recruiting conversion, onboarding lead times, attrition, training capacity, and clinician readiness—and surface risks early enough to act.
  • Build a scalable clinician onboarding model. Partner across Clinical, Talent, IT, Operations, and other teams to evolve today’s high-touch onboarding journey into a structured model that can support significantly larger hiring cohorts without sacrificing clinical quality.
  • Build the leadership capacity required to scale. Determine the right model for preceptors, clinical leads, onboarding cohorts, and frontline management so that rapid growth does not create an unsustainable burden on existing clinical leaders.
  • Own workforce performance management. Establish clear, actionable standards and operating rhythms across areas such as attendance, cancellation rates, Clover Assistant Touch, productivity, and normalized performance measures.
  • Make quality and productivity work together. Build performance expectations that reflect accurate, sustainable clinical performance—not simply higher activity—and partner with clinical leaders to ensure workforce decisions support both member experience and quality of care.
  • Turn workforce data into decisions. Build the dashboards, forecasts, and management routines leaders need to understand capacity, identify constraints, allocate resources, and stay ahead of hiring or performance gaps.
  • Create repeatable workforce-management capabilities for CCS. Use the CCV ramp as the first proving ground for processes, tools, and operating models that can later support In-Home Care and other Clover Care Services programs.
  • Operate as a cross-functional leader. Bring together Clinical Activation, clinical leadership, Talent, Operations, Finance, analytics, and other partners around one integrated workforce plan with clear owners, milestones, and escalation paths.

Success in this role looks like:

In your first 90 days, you will:

  • Build a clear baseline of the CCV workforce funnel and translate the 2027 growth target into a measurable workforce plan spanning recruiting, onboarding, training capacity, clinician readiness, and attrition.
  • Identify the biggest risks and bottlenecks in the ramp and establish the metrics, operating cadence, and accountability needed to address them.

Within your first 6 months, you will:

  • Establish a predictable recruiting-to-readiness operating model, including scalable onboarding cohorts, preceptor capacity, and clinical leadership support.
  • Launch workforce dashboards and performance-management routines that enable leaders to anticipate capacity gaps, manage performance, and increase clinician onboarding volume without sacrificing quality.

Over time, you will:

  • Help CCV reach its clinician-capacity goals ahead of the 2027 AEP cycle through a sustainable, data-driven approach to hiring, onboarding, and performance.
  • Build repeatable workforce-management capabilities that can extend beyond CCV to support In-Home Care and other Clover Care Services programs.

You should get in touch if:

  • You have built or led workforce planning, capacity management, clinical operations, field operations, or another complex people-scaling function where success depended on turning ambitious growth targets into an executable operating plan.
  • You are comfortable owning the full workforce funnel—from recruiting demand and hiring pace through onboarding, readiness, productivity, performance, and attrition.
  • You know how to scale a high-touch operating model without sacrificing the quality, judgment, and human support that made it successful.
  • You are highly analytical and can turn workforce data into useful forecasts, metrics, dashboards, and decisions.
  • You know how to balance productivity with quality, accuracy, and member experience when defining and managing performance.
  • You are an effective cross-functional operator who can create alignment and accountability across clinical leaders, recruiters, operators, analysts, and executives.
  • You are comfortable moving between strategy and execution and thrive in environments where the operating model is still being built.
  • You bring experience scaling distributed clinicians, field teams, home-based care, or another operationally complex healthcare workforce.

Benefits Overview:

  • Financial Well-Being: Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.
  • Physical Well-Being: We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.
  • Mental Well-Being: We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location.
  • Professional Development: Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks:

  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offering discounted equity opportunities
  • Reimbursement for office setup expenses
  • Monthly cell phone & internet stipend
  • Remote-first culture, enabling collaboration with global teams
  • Paid parental leave for all new parents
  • And much more!

About Clover: We are reinventing health insurance by combining the power of data with human empathy to keep our members healthier. We believe the healthcare system is broken, so we've created custom software and analytics to empower our clinical staff to intervene and provide personalized care to the people who need it most.

We always put our members first, and our success as a team is measured by the quality of life of the people we serve. Those who work at Clover are passionate and mission-driven individuals with diverse areas of expertise, working together to solve the most complicated problem in the world: healthcare.

From Clover’s inception, Diversity & Inclusion have always been key to our success. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, perspectives, opinions, and backgrounds, who share a passion for improving people's lives. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employee’s points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We are anE-Verify company.

Final pay is based on several factors including but not limited to internal equity, market data, and the applicant’s education, work experience, certifications, etc.

A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is:
$161,500—$210,000 USD

jobs.description:
SailPoint Engineering Lead, IAM

Location: Dallas, TX | Ashburn, VA | Denver, CO | Charlotte, NC | Boston, MA | New York, NY | Austin, TX ,and open for (Remote)

Your Role

You will serve as the internal owner and technical authority for Digital Realty's SailPoint Identity Security Cloud (ISC) platform, defining how identity governance operates at enterprise scale. This role leads the Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) strategy, architecture, and delivery, ensuring access lifecycle management, certifications, and compliance controls are designed and executed to meet global regulatory and operational requirements. As the enterprise lead for SailPoint ISC, you will drive the evolution of Digital Realty's identity governance program while partnering across Security, Infrastructure, Compliance, and Business teams. This is not an execution role—it is a program leadership position with direct accountability for how identity governance operates across a globally regulated enterprise.

What You'll Do

  • Own and drive the multi-year IGA roadmap and strategy.
  • Define SailPoint ISC architecture across Joiner-Mover-Leaver (JML) lifecycle processes, access certifications, role models, and connectors.
  • Design integrations with Oracle HCM, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, ServiceNow, BeyondTrust, and Microsoft Sentinel.
  • Build and deliver SailPoint ISC capabilities, including workflows, lifecycle rules, access requests, and certification campaigns.
  • Establish configuration-as-code practices utilizing GitHub, CI/CD pipelines, source control, and automated testing as the standard operating model.
  • Lead, mentor, and quality-gate offshore delivery teams.
  • Govern systems integrator (SI) partners and ensure deliverables meet architecture, security, and operational standards.
  • Own SOX User Access Review (UAR) campaigns, audit evidence collection, and compliance engagements.
  • Ensure identity governance controls align with regulatory requirements, including NIS2 and DORA.
  • Define and implement governance for non-human identities, including service accounts, APIs, machine identities, and privileged access integrations.

What You'll Need

  • 8–10 years of Identity and Access Management (IAM) experience, including 4+ years of hands-on SailPoint Identity Security Cloud (IdentityNow) experience.
  • Proven experience designing and implementing end-to-end Joiner-Mover-Leaver (JML) lifecycle processes.
  • Experience owning enterprise IGA architecture and delivering multi-year roadmap initiatives.
  • Strong expertise in access certifications, SOX User Access Reviews (UARs), audit readiness, and compliance engagement.
  • Deep knowledge of non-human identity governance, including service account lifecycle management, NHI discovery and classification, PAM/IGA integration, and secrets management practices.
  • Experience operating identity governance programs within large-scale enterprise environments supporting 10,000+ identities.
  • DevOps mindset with hands-on experience implementing CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and configuration-as-code methodologies.
  • Advanced SailPoint ISC technical expertise, including rules, APIs, connectors, workflows, and integrations.
  • Experience integrating identity platforms with Oracle HCM, Active Directory, and Microsoft Entra ID.

jobs.description:
Product Manager

VA Loan Guaranty (LGY) Program | Full-Time W-2 | Fully Remote (U.S.)

The Problem We're Hiring You to Solve

Every month, your product decisions reach Veterans buying homes, the lenders who close their loans, the servicers who manage them, and the VA staff who stand behind the guaranty.

We are hiring a Product Manager for the modernization of the VA Loan Guaranty (LGY) technology portfolio. The job is translation under pressure: statute, policy, and a sprawling stakeholder ecosystem on one side, a backlog that ships to production every 30 days on the other, while a 20-year-old legacy platform keeps running until the modern one replaces it. If you can hold the Veteran, the lender, and the regulation in your head at the same time, keep reading.

The Opportunity

Most product roles let you invent demand. This one hands you something rarer: a product whose demand is guaranteed by law, which means every ounce of product discipline goes into making the experience better instead of making the funnel bigger.

The LGY portfolio spans the loan guaranty lifecycle: origination-adjacent workflows, servicing oversight and loss mitigation, claims, housing grants, and analytics. The modern platform is Salesforce-centered and configuration-first, supplemented by serverless capabilities in a government cloud. Users include VA program staff and thousands of external lender and servicer users.

The rhythm is fast and formal. Business needs enter through an intake process that produces an executable plan, with refined scope and level of effort, in days. Development runs on a monthly release cadence with an explicit quality bar: acceptance criteria sharp enough to support automated testing, defect detection above 95% before user acceptance testing, and accessibility built into every story. Your requirements are the first link in that quality chain.

You will partner with an Enterprise Solution Architect who owns the designs, an Engineering Lead who owns delivery, and a DevSecOps Lead who owns the platform. You own what gets built, in what order, and why.

What You'll Own

  • The backlog as an instrument of the mission. Turn business needs and policy changes into refined, traceable user stories with acceptance criteria precise enough that engineers build the right thing and testers can automate against it.
  • Intake to executable plan, fast. Drive new needs from raw business intent to a scoped, estimated, committed plan in days, working shoulder to shoulder with architecture and engineering.
  • The roadmap across the portfolio. Sequence modernization, sustainment, and legacy decommissioning, and keep the roadmap credible enough that the customer plans against it.
  • A stakeholder ecosystem, not a stakeholder. Balance VA program officials, field staff, and external lender and servicer users whose interests do not always align.
  • Value in every release. Own prioritization so every 30-day release ships something stakeholders can name, and coordinate user acceptance testing that runs smoothly because the criteria were right from the start.
  • The configure-versus-customize conversation. The program mandates configuration-first solutions. You represent the business value side of those tradeoffs and know when to fight for a custom exception.
  • Decisions informed by data. Ground prioritization in analytics, usage, and operational metrics, and push for instrumentation where it does not exist yet.
  • The transition experience. As functions move from legacy to modern, sequence the change so lenders, servicers, and VA staff are brought along rather than surprised.

AI-Native Product Management

AI is part of how PhoenixTeam works, and product management may have more to gain from it than any other discipline on the program.

We are looking for someone who already uses AI tools as a working part of their practice: analyzing policy and regulation changes to extract requirements impacts in hours instead of weeks, drafting and stress-testing user stories before refinement, synthesizing stakeholder feedback into decision-ready themes, and keeping the backlog coherent as the portfolio grows.

Judgment stays human. You know when AI output misreads a regulation or produces acceptance criteria that sound precise but are not. And boundaries are non-negotiable: federal environments govern what tools may touch government data and systems. Use AI wherever it creates leverage, and understand the security, data, privacy, and authorization boundaries governing where and how it can be used.

What Great Looks Like

Twelve months in, we would expect to see:

  1. Intake is fast and trusted. Needs move from raw intent to committed plans in days, and the customer trusts the scoping because it keeps proving accurate.
  2. Requirements stopped causing rework. Stories flow into development without churn, and ambiguity-driven defects trend toward zero.
  3. Every release has a headline. Stakeholders can name what shipped last month and why it mattered.
  4. UAT is uneventful. The business was engaged all along, not summoned at the end.
  5. The roadmap is the plan of record, and it survives policy changes because you built it to flex.
  6. AI is visibly part of your practice, with policy analysis, story drafting, and feedback synthesis running measurably faster.

What You Bring

We care about evidence more than resumes. Expect us to ask which products you have shaped, what your requirements looked like to the engineers who built from them, and how AI functions in your practice today.

  • A product management record on complex enterprise software, with real users, real stakes, and outcomes rather than ceremonies.
  • Housing finance domain fluency. You can hold your own with business stakeholders on day one. Depth in servicing, loss mitigation, or claims is especially relevant.
  • Requirements craft. You write stories and acceptance criteria that engineers praise and testers can automate against.
  • Federal delivery experience. You treat accessibility, security, and documentation as product constraints to design within, not obstacles to resent.
  • Stakeholder range. You facilitate rooms spanning senior officials, field users, and engineers, and you can say no to a stakeholder and keep the relationship.
  • Evidence-driven prioritization, with stated assumptions when data is thin.
  • Demonstrated AI-in-the-loop practice you can show us concretely.
  • Judgment under ambiguity. You make the call, document the reasoning, and own the outcome.

  • U.S.-based, and able to obtain and maintain a federal Public Trust clearance.

We do not screen on degrees or year counts. If your evidence is strong, we want to talk.

Helpful, Not Required

  • Direct experience with VA Loan Guaranty, VALERI, or other VA benefit programs.
  • FHA, USDA rural housing, or GSE experience, or lender and servicer operations on the commercial side.
  • Product work on Salesforce or a comparable configuration-first platform.
  • Familiarity with MISMO, URLA, Jira and Confluence, or scaled agile.

Leadership Expectations

This role leads through the product. You set direction that architecture, engineering, and the customer align around, present recommendations to federal decision-makers with evidence, and challenge direction that will hurt the program or the Veteran, respectfully and early, including ours. Silent disagreement is a failure mode here, and so is the PM who relays stakeholder requests without shaping them. When priorities conflict, you make the call and own the outcome.

This May Not Be the Role for You If...

You may struggle here if you need someone else to translate policy into requirements, treat product management as ticket administration, avoid telling stakeholders no, wait for complete information before committing, treat compliance as friction rather than product requirements, view AI as a novelty, or stopped learning when you became senior. None of that makes someone a bad product manager. It makes them a bad fit for this particular job.

Why PhoenixTeam

  • You will be among people who speak your language. PhoenixTeam is a woman-owned small business founded and led by housing finance technologists who still do the work, with years embedded inside federal housing programs from loan guaranty to rural housing to mortgage insurance.
  • Direct customer access. Your product judgment reaches the federal decision-makers who act on it.
  • You shape the product, not just the backlog. You define how product management works on this program.
  • AI-native is practice, not positioning. We fund ongoing AI education and development for the entire team.
  • Fully remote,S.-based, permanently.
  • Competitive salary and 100% employer-paid medical insurance.
  • Mission you can explain at dinner. The product you shape supports the home loan benefit for the people who served this country.

Position Requirements

  • Full-time W-2 employment with PhoenixTeam.
  • Must be based in the United States.
  • Fully remote.
  • Work supports the Department of Veterans Affairs Loan Guaranty Service (LGY).
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain the required federal Public Trust clearance. A Secret clearance is not required.

PhoenixTeam is a woman-owned small business focused on federal and commercial housing finance technology.

jobs.excerpt: À propos d’AkinoxAkinox est une entreprise canadienne de santé numérique qui vise à améliorer l’accès des patients aux soins ainsi que la façon dont les organisations de santé les offrent.
jobs.description:
À propos d’Akinox

Akinox est une entreprise canadienne de santé numérique qui vise à améliorer l’accès des patients aux soins ainsi que la façon dont les organisations de santé les offrent. Depuis plus de 15 ans, Akinox collabore avec des organisations de santé et des gouvernements afin de concevoir et d’exploiter des solutions de santé numérique à grande échelle. Nos activités couvrent notamment les soins de première ligne, les soins virtuels, l’accès aux soins et la transformation des processus cliniques.

À propos de CarePath

CarePath transforme des informations cliniques fragmentées en une vue claire et exploitable du patient.

Conçu pour les équipes de soins de première ligne et de santé communautaire, CarePath utilise l’intelligence artificielle pour simplifier l’analyse des dossiers patients, repérer les informations cliniques clés et faciliter la préparation des soins. La solution vise notamment à réduire la charge administrative et clinique liée à l’accueil de nouveaux patients. CarePath entre maintenant dans une phase importante de commercialisation et de développement de sa clientèle.

Le rôle

Nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) Coordonnateur(trice) junior – Développement des affaires et ventes pour soutenir la croissance de CarePath.

Il s’agit d’un contrat de 6 mois à 30 heures par semaine avec possibilité d’extension. La personne recherchée doit avoir un intérêt marqué envers les ventes, le développement commercial, et la technologie dans le domaine de la santé.

En étroite collaboration avec le Chief Growth Officer et l’Architecte de solutions ventes, vous contribuerez à identifier des clients potentiels, à réaliser des activités de prospection, à soutenir les activités de découverte et de vente ainsi qu’à assurer un suivi efficace des occasions d’affaires afin de les faire progresser.

Vos responsabilités

  • Effectuer chaque semaine de la génération de prospects et de la recherche de comptes assistées par l’IA, en fonction des profils de clients idéaux (ICP) définis.
  • Effectuer des recherches sur les organisations de santé ciblées et identifier les décideurs et personnes-ressources pertinents.
  • Créer et maintenir des listes priorisées de prospects et de démarches de prospection.
  • Effectuer de la prospection par courriel, LinkedIn et téléphone en utilisant les messages et campagnes établis pour CarePath.
  • Identifier et communiquer avec les prospects qualifiés ou ayant déjà démontré un intérêt, effectuer une première qualification et coordonner leur transfert à l’Architecte de solutions ventes pour approfondir la découverte des besoins et les discussions entourant la solution.
  • Consigner avec précision dans HubSpot les activités de prospection, les interactions avec les clients, les notes de rencontre, le statut des prospects et les prochaines étapes.
  • Participer aux activités de découverte client, notamment par la recherche sur les comptes, la préparation des rencontres, la prise de notes et les suivis.
  • Contribuer à la préparation et à la personnalisation de présentations de vente, documents synthèses, études de cas et autres outils de vente et de marketing.
  • Interagir avec les clients et les utilisateurs afin de recueillir des commentaires, résultats, données et observations pouvant être utilisés dans les activités de vente et de marketing.
  • Soutenir les webinaires, conférences, lancements de produits et autres activités de mise en marché, notamment en contribuant aux invitations et aux suivis.
  • Fournir au Chief Growth Officer une mise à jour hebdomadaire concise présentant les activités réalisées, les prospects, les rencontres, l’évolution du pipeline de ventes ainsi que les commentaires pertinents provenant du marché.
  • Participer à d’autres activités liées aux ventes, au développement des affaires et à la mise en marché, selon les besoins.

Profil recherché

Il s’agit d’un poste de début de carrière. Nous ne nous attendons donc pas à ce que vous connaissiez déjà tout du secteur de la santé ou de la vente aux entreprises. Nous recherchons plutôt une personne qui :

  • A minimalement un diplôme secondaire, est actuellement aux études (post-secondaire), récemment diplômée ou se situe approximativement dans les cinq premières années de sa carrière.
  • Est à l’aise de communiquer de manière professionnelle par courriel, téléphone et LinkedIn.
  • Est organisée et en mesure d’assurer un suivi rigoureux et constant des activités de prospection et des prochaines étapes.
  • Est à l’aise d’apprendre et d’utiliser des outils d’intelligence artificielle, des plateformes CRM et des outils numériques de vente.
  • Possède de bonnes aptitudes en recherche et est capable de comprendre rapidement une organisation et d’identifier les bonnes personnes à approcher.
  • Possède de bonnes capacités rédactionnelles et peut contribuer à la création de documents professionnels destinés aux clients.
  • Est curieuse, à l’aise de poser des questions et d’interagir avec des professionnels de la santé et des dirigeants d’organisations.
  • Est capable de travailler de manière autonome selon des priorités clairement établies, tout en collaborant étroitement avec une petite équipe.
  • Une expérience avec HubSpot, la vente B2B, le secteur de la santé, la santé numérique, le marketing ou le développement des affaires constitue un atout, mais n’est pas requise.

Ce que vous développerez

Ce rôle vous permettra de participer à l’ensemble du processus de commercialisation d’un produit canadien de santé numérique, de la prospection à la conversion des clients. Vous développerez une expérience pratique en vente B2B, prospection assistée par l’IA, HubSpot et découverte client, tout en collaborant avec des leaders expérimentés. Vous contribuerez également à transformer les besoins et commentaires des clients en stratégies et outils de mise en marché.

------

ENGLISH

About Akinox

Akinox is a Canadian digital health company focused on improving how patients access care and how healthcare organizations deliver it. For more than 15 years, Akinox has worked with healthcare organizations and governments to design and operate digital health solutions at scale. Our work spans primary care, virtual care, patient access and clinical workflow transformation.

About CarePath

CarePath turns fragmented clinical information into a clear, actionable view of the patient.

Designed for primary care and community health teams, CarePath uses artificial intelligence to streamline patient record review, identify key clinical information, and support more efficient care preparation. The solution is designed to reduce the administrative and clinical workload associated with onboarding new patients. CarePath is now entering an important phase of commercialization and customer growth.

The Role

We are looking for an early-career Business Development & Sales Coordinator to support the growth of CarePath.

This is a 6 months contract position at 30 hours per week, with the possibility of extension. We are looking for someone with a strong interest in sales, business development, and technology in the healthcare sector. Working closely with the Chief Growth Officer and Sales Solutions Architect, you will help identify prospective customers, execute outreach, support discovery and sales activities, and ensure opportunities are effectively tracked and advanced.

What You'll Do

  • Conduct weekly AI-assisted lead generation and account research against defined Ideal Customer Profiles (ICPs).
  • Research target healthcare organizations and identify relevant decision-makers and contacts.
  • Build and maintain prioritized prospect and outreach lists.
  • Conduct email, LinkedIn and phone outreach using established CarePath messaging and campaigns.
  • Identify and engage with warm leads, conduct initial qualification and coordinate hand-off to the Sales Solutions Architect for deeper discovery and solution discussions.
  • Accurately record outreach, customer interactions, meeting notes, lead status and next steps in HubSpot.
  • Assist with customer discovery, including account research, meeting preparation, note-taking and follow-up.
  • Help prepare and customize sales decks, one-pagers, case studies and other sales and marketing materials.
  • Interact with customers and users to help capture feedback, results, data points and insights that can be used in sales and marketing.
  • Support webinars, conferences, product launches and other go-to-market activities, including invitations and follow-up.
  • Provide a concise weekly update to the Chief Growth Officer covering activity, leads, meetings, pipeline movement and relevant market feedback.
  • Assist with other sales, business development and go-to-market activities as required.

What We're Looking For

This is an early-career role, so we don't expect you to arrive knowing everything about healthcare or enterprise sales. We are looking for someone who is:

  • Has at least a high school diploma and is currently pursuing post-secondary studies, has recently graduated, or is approximately within the first five years of their career.
  • Comfortable communicating professionally by email, phone and LinkedIn.
  • Organized and able to consistently follow through on outreach and next steps.
  • Comfortable learning and using AI tools, CRM platforms and digital sales tools.
  • A strong researcher who can quickly understand an organization and identify the right people to approach.
  • Able to write clearly and help create professional customer-facing materials.
  • Curious and comfortable asking questions and interacting with healthcare professionals and organizational leaders.
  • Able to work independently within clear priorities while collaborating closely with a small team.

Experience with HubSpot, B2B sales, healthcare, digital health, marketing or business development is an asset, but not required.

What You'll Gain

This role will allow you to participate in the entire commercialization process of a Canadian digital health product, from prospecting to customer conversion. You will gain hands-on experience in B2B sales, AI-assisted prospecting, HubSpot, and customer discovery while working alongside experienced leaders. You will also contribute to transforming customer needs and feedback into go-to-market strategies and sales tools.

  • Analyze business requirements and design scalable SAP MM solutions supporting procurement and supply chain operations.

How We Thrive

At Panopto, we believe in simple elegance in everything we do. We do not just talk about accountability; we live it. You will be joining a collaborative team of seasoned Account Executives and Revenue leaders who are deeply embedded in the enterprise sector.

As Director, Industry Practice Lead, you will be the bridge between technical capability and business transformation. This is an opportunity to serve as a trusted advisor to key buyers, shape our go-to-market strategy, and serve as the voice of the customer back to our Product and Engineering teams.

The Foundation for Success

What Sets You Apart

Join Us

Join Panopto and play a pivotal role in transforming how enterprise organizations capture, share, and scale workforce knowledge. If you are a seasoned L&D and technology leader ready to drive executive engagement and accelerate growth across Fortune 500 accounts, we encourage you to apply.

Total Rewards

The salary range for this position is $160,000 - $200,000 USD per year. This position is also eligible for a bonus as part of the compensation package.

Base pay offered may vary depending on various factors, including, but not limited to: job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and other eligibility factors such as geographic location. The Total Rewards package includes competitive base pay and an opportunity to enroll in a variety of benefit programs such as health insurance, flexible spending accounts, retirement savings plans, life and disability insurance programs, and programs that provide for both paid and unpaid time away from work. At Panopto, we know that great people make an organization great. We value our people and offer employees benefits that are market competitive for our industry. Learn more about what working at Panopto can mean for you.

At Panopto, our commitment to pay equity and transparency is unwavering. We do not engage in salary negotiations beyond the established range to maintain fairness and prevent potential pay disparities among team members based on negotiation strategies.

Beyond the Requirements: At this point, we hope you're feeling excited about the job description you’re reading. Even if you don't feel that you meet every single requirement, we still encourage you to apply. We're eager to meet people that believe in our mission and can contribute to our team in a variety of ways - not just candidates who check all the boxes. We want people to feel comfortable expressing their true selves and to come, stay, and do their best work here.

Recruiting Tips: From crafting an impressive resume to presenting your best self during our interviews, we're dedicated to ensuring you feel well-prepared and self-assured as you embark on opportunities at Panopto. Discover some valuableRecruiting Tipsfrom our team.

Our people and culture

Panopto’s mission is to be the leader in visual and audio-based learning in a capture and post-capture world. Our user base is as diverse as the world’s universities and businesses. Panopto’s commitment to fostering a fair, equitable, and inclusive culture empowers each member of our team to express their authentic selves, contribute their distinct perspectives and make a meaningful impact both individually and collectively. This collaborative spirit empowers us to challenge ideas (not people) recognizing that our shared success relies on collective wisdom. It drives us to continuously improve and innovate, ultimately elevating the quality of our products and services. It’s what sets Panopto apart as a unique and rewarding place to work.

Our purpose

We believe that video can have a transformative effect on learning. So we built a video knowledge management platform that helps businesses and universities improve the way that they train, teach, and share knowledge. Since 2007, we have been a pioneer in video capture software, video management, and inside-video-search technology. Panopto has been adopted by more than 1,600 companies and universities worldwide with over 11 million end users. Today, Panopto’s knowledge management platform is the largest repository of expert learning videos in the world. A proud remote-first company, Panopto is headquartered in Pittsburgh, with offices in London, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Sydney, and has received industry recognition for its innovation, rapid growth, and company culture.

Panopto is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

We value and encourage diversity and solicit applications from all qualified individuals which will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability or protected veteran status, or any other legally protected criteria, in accordance with applicable law. Panopto is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to applicants with disabilities. If you require accommodation for interviewing or otherwise participating in the employee selection process, please provide more detail on how we can further support you by reaching out to the Employee Experience department.

Remote, US: Candidates looking for flexible or remote-friendly positions are encouraged to apply. Panopto is proud to be a remote-first company. Employees in this position are eligible to work remotely.

Remote, International: Candidates looking for flexible or remote-friendly positions are encouraged to apply. Panopto is proud to be a remote-first company. Employees in this position are eligible to work remotely. Still, they may make regular trips to the local international office from time to time, where applicable.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Panopto AI Use Policy:

Panopto’s AI Use Policy is committed to a hiring process that is thoughtful, fair, and centered on human connection. As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more prevalent in the workplace, we believe that it is important to describe our use of AI in the hiring process, as well as outline to candidates what use of AI is and is not allowed. While AI can be a valuable tool, it cannot replace genuine human interaction or an individual’s unique perspective, experience, and voice.

Company Use of AI:

Panopto may utilize tools to enhance the efficiency, objectivity, and quality of our recruitment and evaluation process. These tools assist our team throughout the hiring lifecycle by focusing on four key areas:

  • Content Creation: Providing a starting point for crafting job descriptions and assisting in building tailored interview questions.

  • Resume Parsing: Analyzing candidate skillsets and resume alignment to efficiently identify qualified candidates.

  • Interview & Assessment Insights: Providing interview transcription, summarization, and identifying key insights from candidate assessments in relation to specific role requirements.

  • Data Organization: Organizing and storing information gathered during assessments to help our team make informed, data-driven decisions.

Ultimately, these tools are used to support—not replace—our team in assessing skills, generating insights, and identifying the best talent for Panopto.

To ensure fairness and transparency:

Human-Centric Decisions: Please be assured that AI tools are used to support our team, and all final hiring decisions are made by human reviewers. Panopto hiring teams will thoroughly review your application and assessment results. AI is not used to make final decisions regarding your candidacy.

Bias Mitigation: We are committed to algorithmic fairness. Our AI-assisted tools undergo regular independent audits to detect and mitigate bias, with the goal of keeping our processes equitable and inclusive. Our methodology aligns with global best practices and regional digital ethics standards to provide every candidate with a fair and merit-based evaluation.

Your Rights & Accommodations: We provide inclusive access for all applicants. If you require a reasonable adjustment due to a disability, or if you prefer a non-automated review of your application, please contact Panopto Talent Attraction. We respect your right to request human intervention; please note that opting for a manual review may impact the standard processing timeline.

Data Privacy and Security:

Your personal data and recordings are processed securely in compliance with global privacy and employment regulations (including EEOC, GDPR, and other local or regional privacy laws, as applicable).

To facilitate our recruitment and evaluation process, limited candidate data may be shared securely with trusted third-party vendors and service providers acting on our behalf. We retain candidate data only as long as necessary to fulfill the recruitment purpose or as required by applicable statutory retention periods. Once this purpose is met, or the retention period expires, your data is securely deleted or anonymized in accordance with our data governance policy.

Panopto is dedicated to a fair and equitable hiring process for all candidates.

Use of AI:

Statement of Transparency:

At Panopto, we embrace the transformative power of AI to enhance productivity and learning. We believe in providing a level playing field where candidates can use modern tools to put their best foot forward, provided those tools support, rather than replace, their authentic voice and expertise. While we encourage the use of AI as a tool for growth and preparation, we require transparency and authenticity to ensure a fair evaluation for all.

Acceptable Use:

  • AI-Assisted Preparation: You are encouraged to use Generative AI (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini) as a mock interviewer or coach to refine your speaking points.

  • Research & Knowledge Gathering: Using AI to synthesize industry trends or company background is permitted and viewed as proactive preparation.

  • Career Guidance Tools: Simulation tools that help you practice the STAR method or identify skill gaps are acceptable.

Prohibited Use:

  • Live Interview Assistance: The use of real-time AI "teleprompters," live answer-generators, or deepfake audio/video during Panopto recordings or live sessions is strictly prohibited.

  • Plagiarized Work Samples: Any take-home assignments or portfolios must be your original work. While AI can assist in formatting or brainstorming, the core logic and execution must be yours.

Panopto has a zero-tolerance policy toward the misrepresentation of job-related skills. Consequences of using prohibited tools may result in my immediate disqualification from the hiring process, the withdrawal of any pending offer, or termination of employment if discovered after hire.

Verification of Experience:

To ensure the integrity of our hiring process and validate the skills demonstrated during your Panopto submission, Panopto may require the following "Proof of Experience":

  • Work Samples & Portfolios: Candidates may be asked to provide original work samples (e.g., code repositories, design portfolios, case studies) that pre-date the current application.

  • Digital Footprint & Professional Links: We may request links to professional profiles (e.g., LinkedIn, GitHub, Behance) to verify career trajectory and industry contributions.

Disclosures:

  • Live Validation: Any technical skill demonstrated in an asynchronous Panopto recording is subject to a live, "Human-in-the-Loop" technical assessment or deep-dive discussion.

  • Fraud Detection: Please be aware that we utilize metadata analysis and fraud detection tools to ensure the authenticity of all video submissions.

By submitting your application and participating in the recruitment process, you acknowledge and consent to Panopto's use of AI, as well as the acceptable and prohibited uses of AI as a candidate, as described above.

Panopto is dedicated to a fair and equitable hiring process for all candidates.

Scientific Safety Alliance, or SSA, exists to Accelerate Science. Delightfully. In just over three years, SSA has created over $300M in enterprise value through disciplined growth and 21 acquisitions. We are now intentionally building the executive leadership team that will take SSA to $1B+ in enterprise value.

We serve the life sciences world — pharmaceutical, biotech, hospital, and research facilities — by removing operational friction so innovation can move faster. SSA is a 100% founder- and employee-owned company, and ownership is real: performance directly compounds value for every team member.

jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato.

YOUR ROLE

You'll build the models that decide which carrier each auto insurance shopper sees on our click wall. The goal is to send every user to the carrier most likely to convert them, so carriers see our traffic convert and raise their bids. You'll also own the buying models behind our media spend, which are held to ROAS.

Carrier conversion data (quotes, policies and acquisition cost) is now coming back to us, and you'll be the one who puts it to work in production. The hard part is the data. Outcomes land weeks or months after the click, many sessions are sparse, the same shoppers come back, and the market drifts. Our bids also decide which users we win, so the model shapes the data it learns from next.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You frame problems directly with the business, find your own data, build and validate the model, and stay with it through deployment and monitoring. An ML engineer works alongside you on the production side. Auto insurance takes most of your time to start, and scope broadens to other verticals over time.

We're remote first, and most of the company works East Coast hours.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

By day 60, you run our insurance marketplace media buying on your own.

By the end of your first year:

  • Click wall serving that matches each user to the right carrier
  • Carrier conversion data running in production models
  • Automated marketplace bidding taken from proof of concept to scale
  • A clear approach for repeat users and sparse sessions
  • Production models that hold up through drift and changing objectives
  • Output the business trusts and uses without rework

MUST HAVE

  • 5+ years of hands-on applied data science with measurable business impact
  • Your models drove paid media decisions: spend, bidding or ad serving. Attribution and reporting alone don't qualify.
  • You built what's on your resume and can explain it down to the loss function and architecture choice, neural network fundamentals included
  • You see how today's bids shape tomorrow's training data, and you've handled late labels, sparse features or drift
  • You own models end to end: you find your own data, build through deployment and monitoring, and bring a point of view
  • Expert Python and SQL

NICE TO HAVES

  • Real ad budget spent in live auctions
  • Large-scale ranking or recommendation systems
  • Explaining tradeoffs to non-technical partners in plain terms
  • Designing for auction feedback loops, selection bias and exploration
  • Hands-on neural network work, such as embeddings of text, creative or user behavior
  • AWS for data science: ECS, S3, Athena, SageMaker
  • CI/CD deployment

Want to accelerate your career? Apply now!

We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

You’ll find upsell and cross-sell opportunities, build the business case with your champion, and close.

Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a SLED Solutions Architect, you'll be a trusted technical advisor to State, Local, and Education customers in every state east of the Mississippi River: state agencies, counties, cities, special districts, community colleges, and public, private, and research universities. These organizations deliver services residents and students rely on every day, often with lean IT teams, aging systems, fixed fiscal-year budgets, and growing cybersecurity threats.

You'll show them how GitLab's DevSecOps platform and AI capabilities, including the GitLab Duo Agent Platform, help them modernize legacy applications, protect sensitive resident and student data, meet state and sector compliance requirements, and do more with the staff they have. You'll own the technical evaluation and validation stages of the sales cycle, guide customers through proofs of concept and value, and translate platform capabilities into outcomes that agency leaders, CIOs, CISOs, and procurement officers can defend in a budget request or an RFP evaluation.

You'll partner closely with SLED account executives, channel partners, and systems integrators, provide technical guidance from first conversation through successful deployment, and bring the voice of the SLED customer back into Product, Sales, and Marketing.

Location and travel: The territory covers all states east of the Mississippi River. The candidate must reside in the Northeast part of the United States. This role requires up to 50% travel.

What you'll do

  • Engage SLED customers onsite and remotely, from state capitals to university campuses, with tailored demos, technical presentations, and hands-on workshops that tie GitLab to their mission.
  • Partner with SLED account executives to shape account strategies that align with each customer's fiscal year budget cycle, legislative appropriations, IT modernization plans, and grant or federal pass through funding.
  • Own the technical evaluation process, including proof of concept (POC) and proof of value (POV) design and delivery, and provide technical responses for RFIs, RFPs, RFQs, and security questionnaires.

  • Guide customers through state and sector security requirements, such as GovRAMP and NIST frameworks, and show how GitLab's built in security, auditability, and deployment options reduce compliance burden.
  • Help agencies and institutions modernize legacy and mainframe applications, such as unemployment insurance, tax, DMV, benefits, and student information systems, using GitLab and AI-assisted development to lower risk and offset shrinking pools of legacy skilled staff.
  • Advise customers on adopting AI responsibly, including the GitLab Duo Agent Platform, in line with state AI policies, governance boards, and data privacy requirements.
  • Lead the creation of Customer Success Plans that capture technical success criteria and handoff details, ensuring a smooth path to deployment and adoption, often for IT teams with limited capacity.
  • Work alongside Account Executives to build data driven business cases that quantify delivery bottlenecks, giving customers a defensible basis for budget requests and clear evidence of return on taxpayer investment.
  • Build relationships with CIOs, CISOs, agency directors, enterprise architects, faculty, research computing leaders, and procurement officers so they become advocates for GitLab, including across agencies and campuses that share services.
  • Collaborate with systems integrators and state IT shared-services organizations to scale GitLab adoption across multiple agencies, local governments, or campuses.
  • Serve as the SLED customer advocate internally, channeling feedback on procurement, compliance, and deployment needs to Product, Sales, and Marketing.
  • Stay current on GitLab and related technologies, and create reusable SLED demos, reference architectures, and assets for customers and partners.

What you'll bring

  • Background in technical pre-sales, consulting, or IT roles serving state agencies, local governments, or public, private, and research universities, where you guided customers through evaluations and solution design.
  • Working knowledge of how SLED organizations buy technology: RFP and RFI cycles, cooperative purchasing agreements, statewide contracts, fiscal-year budgeting, and the role of resellers and systems integrators.
  • Hands-on experience using GitLab and familiarity with modern software development and operations practices, such as CI/CD, DevSecOps, and automation.

  • Familiarity with security and compliance frameworks common in SLED, such as GovRAMP and NIST SP 800-53.
  • Ability to connect technical solutions to mission outcomes, such as resident service delivery, cyber resilience, cost avoidance, and workforce efficiency, and to advise senior stakeholders on tradeoffs and options.
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills, including presenting to both technical teams and non-technical leaders such as agency heads, procurement officers, and university administrators.
  • Openness to learning, seeking feedback, and building new skills, including familiarity with GitLab's Solutions Architect handbook and related resources.

Nice to have

  • Prior experience working in or for state or local government IT, or a university IT or research computing organization.
  • Experience with legacy or mainframe modernization programs.
  • Familiarity with AI governance practices in the public sector, such as AI use-case inventories, acceptable-use policies, and risk assessments.

About the team

The SLED Solutions Architect role is part of GitLab's Public Sector Solutions Architect team, a group of trusted technical advisors who help government and education customers understand, evaluate, and adopt the GitLab DevSecOps platform. The team is distributed and collaborates asynchronously across time zones using GitLab and our handbook-first practices to share knowledge, reusable examples, and best practices.

On the SLED team, you'll help customers solve challenges unique to state, local, and education organizations: protecting resident and student data, modernizing mission-critical legacy systems, buying through public procurement processes, and stretching limited IT staff and budgets. About Us

Thimble was an early pioneer in insurtech. That gives us something rare: the speed, ownership and culture of a startup, with the balance sheet, stability and long-term commitment of one of the industry’s strongest insurers.
For more information, visit thimble.com.

Our Values

Our unique culture is built around our six core values:

Think Wild, Act Tame

Be relentlessly creative. Question everything. Get to know the rules so well, you can use them in new ways. Be the industry’s compliant radicals.

Green Means GO

Act. Move forward. Learn. You can only make a decision based on the best information you have – so make it.

Own Every Detail

Be ruthlessly precise. Disciplined. Sweat the small stuff.
Simplify, Simplify, Simplify
Get to the point. Make it crystal clear. Cut everything else. It’s our job to make insurance easy – however hard that is for us.

Every Moment Counts

Show up early and ready. Deliver on time or before. Make the most of your time, so others can make the most of theirs.

Stay Human

Treat every person, and their ideas, with respect. Cherish diversity.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Senior Vice President of Broker Distribution to lead Thimble’s next stage of growth within the broker channel. With a proven platform, expanding technology and AI native capabilities, the focus is on scaling our broker and distribution partner network to increase premium. About VisiQuate

VisiQuate is a healthcare revenue cycle intelligence company. We help health systems and revenue cycle services organizations improve financial performance with analytics, automation and AI. We are building a new generation of AI-native products that work inside our clients' revenue cycle workflows, and we are growing the team that builds them.

The role: run your service line like a general manager

You will own a portfolio of AI-native revenue cycle products as if it were your own business. That means more than features and a backlog. You are accountable for whether your service line wins in the market, delivers cash outcomes for clients, and grows profitably.

In practice, you are the person in the company who knows your area best:

  • The market, the buyers, and every client problem worth solving
  • Every competitor, including what Epic and other EHRs are building, and how we beat them
  • What it costs us to deliver, and what clients will pay
  • Whether each pilot is succeeding, and why
  • How Sales should pitch it and how Marketing should frame it

You lead through influence across Engineering, Data Science, Customer Success, Sales and Marketing. Nobody reports to you on those teams, but your service line's results are yours.

What you'll own

Market and clients

  • Know your market inside and out: segments, buyers, budgets, buying cycles, and the regulatory and payer changes that reshape it.
  • Maintain a living map of client challenges in your area, ranked by the cash and effort at stake, and know which ones we solve today.
  • Spend time in client workflows. Build a client advisory group and keep a steady stream of interviews and site visits.
  • Be the voice of the client inside VisiQuate, backed by evidence rather than anecdotes.

Competition and ecosystem

  • Track every competitor in your space: their products, pricing, wins, losses and direction. Know how we beat each one.
  • Know what Epic, Oracle Health and other EHR vendors are building that overlaps with us, and where we complement rather than compete.
  • Define how we sell into clients on advanced EHRs like Epic: integration paths, marketplace programs, and the case for VisiQuate alongside native tools.
  • Watch payer, clearinghouse and partner moves that create threats or openings. Recommend build, buy or partner when it fits.
  • Run win and loss reviews and turn them into roadmap and positioning changes.

Strategy and economics

  • Own the vision, strategy and roadmap for your service line, from first release through later versions.
  • Build the business case before development, with outcomes measured in cash: cash recovered, avoidable denials, touches per claim, cost to collect, days to resolution.
  • Recommend pricing and packaging for approval by the EVP and Growth leadership. Know the value we create per client and what the market will bear.
  • Know your cost drivers: AI inference, clearinghouse and transaction fees, data and infrastructure, implementation and support effort. Design products and prices that protect margin.
  • Make disciplined trade-offs on client value, differentiation, commercial impact and cost, and say no clearly.

Build and deliver

  • Write specifications, business rules, acceptance criteria and non-functional requirements that work for both engineers and AI development tools.
  • Keep the Product Roadmap current and tie every development task to a roadmap feature.
  • Build on our shared platform and canonical data model, and reuse shared services rather than rebuilding them.
  • Lead Agile delivery with your engineering partners: refinement, planning, demos, release and post-launch measurement.
  • Modernize existing capabilities into new products while protecting the experience of current clients.

AI quality, safety and compliance

  • Set evaluation criteria for AI and agentic features: accuracy, task completion, reliability, latency and cost.
  • Define permissions, escalation and human oversight for agent actions on client systems, such as appeals, rebills, payer portals and EHR updates.
  • Work with Security and Legal on PHI handling, auditability and BAAs.

Pilots and client outcomes

  • Own every pilot in your portfolio end to end: success criteria, data readiness, implementation plan, weekly check-ins and go-live.
  • Prove ROI per client in cash, and turn successful pilots into references and case studies.
  • Own client outcomes through renewal and expansion with Customer Success, including adoption, escalations and the support playbook.

Go-to-market

  • Build demos that client-facing teams use to win, defend and expand accounts.
  • Train Sales on how to pitch your products, handle objections and position against competitors. Join strategic deals when it matters.
  • Work with Marketing on positioning, messaging, launch plans, case studies and thought leadership.
  • Represent your service line externally at client forums, industry events and with analysts.

Business reviews

  • Run a regular business review of your service line: pipeline, revenue, margin, adoption, client outcomes and delivery health.
  • Report to leadership with clear asks, risks and decisions needed.

How you'll work

You run our Product Development Lifecycle with AI built into every phase and a human accountable at every gate. AI should accelerate the lifecycle, not replace its discipline.

  • Use AI for discovery, research synthesis, specifications, prototyping and analysis, and hold its output to enterprise standards.
  • Build working demos and prototypes yourself with AI tools such as Claude Code, so ideas reach clients in days rather than months.
  • For new products, follow our path from concept pitch to demos, a pilot client, go-live and general availability, with the prospect pipeline built in parallel.
  • Keep your service line's product home current in Notion and its roadmap current in GitHub, so anyone in the company can see where things stand.

What success looks like in your first year

  • You can brief the executive team on your market, competitors and EHR landscape without notes.
  • Your service line has an approved strategy, a business case, and a roadmap tied to cash outcomes.
  • At least one pilot is live, measured, and producing a referenceable ROI story.
  • Sales can demo and pitch your products confidently without you in the room.
  • Pricing reflects both client value and our cost to deliver, and margin is tracked.
  • You run a regular business review that leadership uses to make decisions.

Requirements

  • Required: 7+ years of hands-on healthcare revenue cycle experience as a subject matter expert, with depth in one or more of: denials and appeals, patient access and financial clearance, payment integrity and underpayments, A/R follow-up, payer contracts and policy.
  • 8+ years of Product Management on complex SaaS or enterprise products, with clear ownership of business results. Senior Director candidates: experience leading Product Managers and multiple product lines.
  • Working knowledge of 837/835 data, CARC/RARC codes and EHR workflows (Epic, Oracle Health/Cerner).
  • Experience with AI/ML, automation or agentic products, and direct use of AI prototyping tools.
  • Experience owning pricing, packaging or a business case through to revenue.
  • Strong technical fluency to partner with engineers, data scientists and architects.
  • Strong understanding of SaaS economics: adoption, retention, expansion and margin.
  • Comfort in front of clients, Sales and executives, and a mindset that combines speed with rigor.

Our Founding Principles

Successful candidates will value and embrace VisiQuate's Founding Principles:

  • Leadership: We lead by example and by empowering our clients, partners and staff.
  • Optimism: Our glass is decidedly half full, and then some.
  • Curiosity: We approach the who, what, where, when, why and how questions with an inquisitiveness that delights in discovering fresh ideas.
  • Zeal: We approach our work with eagerness, determination and contagious enthusiasm.
  • Integrity: We value conscience, character, truth and honor as fundamental principles.
  • Innovation: We believe in a continuous and relentless pursuit of all that seems unimaginable.
  • Fun: We believe that hard work and fun go hand in hand.
  • Compassion: We lead not only with our heads, but with our hearts.
  • Giving: We gladly give our time and money to causes we believe in.

jobs.description:
Fieldstone A&E - Creating Community

Fieldstone A&E is an industry-leading company with deep roots in home building by providing everything needed for vertical construction, from single-family homes to clubhouses, commercial buildings and everything in between. You will feel like family in our rich company culture that focuses on work/life integration with flexible work capabilities by offering remote, in-office and hybrid situations. We promote many team development opportunities such as daily huddles, virtual and in-person Happy Hour events, Weekly Lunchtime Trivia, and Team-Building events that bring team members together from other locations. Our attractive benefits package includes 401k, profit sharing, and shared health, dental, and vision costs.

With offices located in Metro Detroit and Tampa, we have the flexibility of in-office employment as well as the option for remote. The candidate we’re looking for has an exceptional ability to focus in a bustling team environment, and utilize strong time management skills, while occasionally tending to multiple projects at once, ensuring they are of the highest quality once completed. Our candidate must possess and exhibit a positive, “can-do” attitude even in high-stress situations, with an unwavering commitment to “world-class customer service”. Our company has shifted to an almost fully remote workforce, so we understand the need for a flexible schedule. We’re looking for someone who holds our company values close to heart: being passionate about what they do, are actively open-minded, showing dedication to mastering their craft, and above all, embracing family spirit. If these values describe you, we would love to have you join our team!

Synopsis

The Truss Repair Designer works in partnership with clients, Component Manufacturers, Architects, Engineers, and field personnel to develop clear and accurate repair designs for roof and floor trusses and related engineered wood products. Using photographs, field reports, truss design documents, and construction documents, this role evaluates field conditions and repair needs, prepares repair drawings and supporting calculations, and communicates technical requirements to clients and project partners. The Truss Repair Designer manages multiple repair projects while adhering to applicable building codes, design standards, client requirements, and Fieldstone quality standards.

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Design repairs for residential and commercial roof and floor trusses and related engineered wood products based on photographs, field reports, truss design documents, and construction documents.
  • Prepare clear and accurate truss repair drawings, details, and supporting calculations for field use and review.
  • Review damaged, altered, or nonconforming truss conditions and develop appropriate repair solutions based on the available field and design information.
  • Review construction documents and truss design drawings for accuracy, design requirements, and code compliance.
  • Determine repair design requirements using structural principles including roof and floor loading, load paths, wood member design, and wood connector design.
  • Calculate and evaluate tributary loads, concentrated loads, and load transfer as applicable to the repair condition.
  • Use MiTek SE and other applicable truss engineering software to analyze truss conditions and develop repair designs.
  • Communicate with clients to obtain missing information, clarify field conditions, answer technical questions, and communicate repair requirements.
  • Communicate with the Architect or Engineer when technical clarification or engineering review is required.
  • Manage multiple repair projects at one time, prioritize workload, and maintain project status in order to meet deadlines.
  • Maintain job-related files utilizing Fieldstone file and folder structure processes and procedures.
  • Consistently apply Fieldstone Quality Control procedures and take ownership of the accuracy and completeness of work.
  • Maintain and comply with Fieldstone and client-specific standards, including CAD, file management, and documentation requirements.
  • Foster a culture of external and internal client service.
  • Other duties may be assigned.

Required Knowledge

  • Knowledge of wood truss systems, truss products, metal plate connected trusses, connectors, and related engineered wood products.
  • Working familiarity with building codes and design standards, including the International Residential Code (IRC), International Building Code (IBC), ASCE 7, National Design Specification (NDS) for Wood Construction, and ANSI/TPI standards.
  • Solid understanding of structural principles including residential and commercial roof and floor loading, load paths, wood member design, and wood connector design.
  • Strong mathematical abilities, including the ability to calculate tributary loads, concentrated loads, and load transfer throughout the building.
  • Ability to read and review blueprints, architectural drawings, construction documents, truss design drawings, and field reports.
  • Knowledge of residential and commercial construction as it relates to truss design and repair conditions.

Required Skills

  • Ability to develop clear, practical truss repair solutions from photographs, field reports, truss design documents, and other available project information.
  • Working knowledge of MiTek SE or similar metal plate connected truss engineering software.
  • Ability to prepare clear repair drawings, details, calculations, and technical documentation.
  • Familiarity with AutoCAD is preferred.
  • Strong technical writing and verbal communication skills for repair drawings, calculations, and client correspondence.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to identify discrepancies or missing information that may affect a repair design.
  • Ability to manage and successfully prioritize multiple projects at one time.
  • Ability to work independently and complete assignments in a timely manner with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with clients and project partners regarding technical and field-related repair questions.
  • Consistent ability to successfully meet deadlines.

Required Experience

  • 3+ years of experience in wood truss design and engineering software.
  • Direct experience designing truss repairs is strongly preferred.
  • A degree in civil or structural engineering is preferred but not required.
  • Experienced truss designers with strong practical knowledge are encouraged to apply, as are designers with an engineering background who want to learn truss repair design.
  • Computer-aided drafting experience preferred.

We weave AI into the fabric of everything we do and use it to augment the impact every individual can have. If you are passionate about solving real-world problems and ideating beside the best and the brightest, we invite you to join us!

This role is remote, but distance is no barrier to impact. Our hybrid teams collaborate across geographies to solve big problems, stay close to our customers, and grow together. You will be part of a culture that values trust, accountability, and shared success where your work truly matters.

Your Career

jobs.excerpt: ABOUT THE ROLEAI is rewriting how every company works, and everyone is racing to figure out how to secure it.
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

AI is rewriting how every company works, and everyone is racing to figure out how to secure it. We have, and we need someone to take it to market.

The AI Security Sales Executive is a quota-carrying sales role dedicated entirely to Abnormal's AI Security suite: five products built to help customers govern AI, secure AI, and defend against rogue AI. You will own AI Security in your territory, from the first conversation through close, hunting the largest new logos while working alongside the Account Executives who already know our customers best. This is a sales role for someone who can carry a number and go as deep technically as our best engineers when a conversation demands it.

The timing matters. Abnormal is growing about 50% year over year, with more than 5,000 customers and over 30% of the Fortune 500 trusting us to protect their people. AI security now comes up in close to 80% of customer conversations at the executive level, and customers already trust our behavioral AI to solve it. Demand is outrunning capacity. You will step into a deep pipeline on day one, and you will have real say in how this category gets sold.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own AI Security in your territory. Carry the AI Security quota and run the full sales cycle end to end, from first conversation through close, including significant upsell campaigns across our existing customer base.
  • Hunt the largest new logos. Take Abnormal's AI Security story into the biggest enterprises in the world, and open doors beyond the customers who already trust us.
  • Prioritize ruthlessly. Inbound interest will outpace your calendar. Decide where your time moves the needle, and where it does not.
  • Partner with Account Executives. Work alongside the core team in your territory, equip them to carry AI Security conversations, and step in on the deals that matter most.
  • Go deep on the technology. Hold your own with security and platform teams on behavioral AI, cloud security, and agent security when a customer needs more than a standard pitch.
  • Run point on design partner conversations for products still in early availability, working closely with product leadership to shape these deals and bring the right resources to the table.
  • Shape the product and the playbook. Feed what you hear in the field back to product leadership in a fast loop, and help build how AI Security gets sold as the suite matures from early availability to GA.
  • Stay current as the suite evolves. Availability and depth will shift quickly, and you will keep pace.

WHAT YOU’LL SELL

Abnormal's AI Security suite includes five products, each at a different stage of availability:

  • AI Governance: Discovers your AI, uncovers shadow AI, and shows who's using what and at what cost.
  • AI Cloud Security: Detects and contains AI cloud breaches using behavioral AI and honeypots.
  • AI Employee Guardrails: Lets employees use AI without leaking data or triggering unintended actions.
  • AI Agent Security: Inventories an organization's AI agents and ensures they behave as intended.
  • AI Security Workbench: Lets security teams use AI to run investigations with Abnormal's models, without guardrails.

WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS RIGHT NOW

Every security vendor is staking a claim in AI security. Abnormal has earned real credibility here through eight years of behavioral AI investment and a track record protecting email for thousands of customers. That trust is an advantage today, not a permanent one, and this role exists to make sure we capitalize on it while the window is open.

For the right person, that means owning a brand-new motion at the center of a fast-growing company, working directly with executive and product leadership, and building a track record as one of the people who defined how this category gets sold.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 5+ years of quota-carrying sales experience, primarily selling into Enterprise accounts, with a proven record of winning new logos and expanding accounts.
  • Technical depth and curiosity: comfort discussing AI architecture, cloud security concepts, and how behavioral models work, in enough detail to earn trust with technical buyers.
  • A hunter's drive paired with the judgment to prioritize when demand exceeds capacity.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity. The suite and the motion for selling it are still evolving, and much of the playbook will be written by whoever takes this role on.
  • Strong cross-functional instincts. You will partner closely with Account Executives, Sales Engineering, and product leadership, and you will work autonomously between those touchpoints.

NICE TO HAVES

  • Direct experience selling AI security, cloud security, or other emerging security categories.
  • Experience in an overlay, specialist, or advisory role in cybersecurity or AI, or a record of selling into CISOs and security leaders.
  • Experience selling early-availability products and shaping design partner deals.

Actual compensation will be determined based on several non-discriminatory factors including skills, experience, qualifications, and geographic location.
In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for bonus or incentive compensation, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package.
